description: March Run 8 is part of the Oslo Running Festival, which consists of eight races along the capital's beautiful trails and scenic roads. The race can be completed at any time, either alone in the SOLO category or in a team competition as a DUO or TRIO. Each race is scheduled to start on a Friday at 12:00 PM, and the course is open until Sunday at 11:00 AM the following weekend. Distances of 5 and 10 km are offered, running on certified courses.

The race takes place in Ringsaker, Hedmark, and has a distance of 6.9 kilometers. This year's event is particularly important due to many canceled opportunities for fitness and competitions, gathering around 100 participants each time, despite varying weather conditions. Participants are required to wear reflective vests and demonstrate traffic awareness, with options for both timed and fitness classes.

The courses are officially measured, and participants have the opportunity to set personal records. There were reports of 380 registered participants and enough medals for everyone.

The event warmly welcomes all ambitions, whether you walk, power walk, jog, or run. Hamarkarusellen Winter consists of 6 races from October to March, providing an excellent opportunity to use as a test race. After the races, juice (and often cake!) is served at the finish area, contributing to community and fun.

name: Sandnes Backyard
description: The Backyard concept involves running a loop of 6.7 km or 4.167 miles every hour. Sandnes Backyard is intended as a social low-threshold race, and it is entirely up to each individual whether they want to run 1, 2, or all 12 laps, thus finishing at 50 miles or 80 km. Each lap starts on the hour, so it's important to find the right strategy. The faster you run, the longer break you get between laps, and Sandnes Arena serves as a break room where participants can warm up and discuss the race.
course_highlights: Sandnes Backyard is intended as a social low-threshold race.
Each lap starts at the top of the hour, so it's important to find the right strategy.

Participants can choose between several distances: half marathon, 10 km, 5 km, and a children's race. The courses traverse beautiful surroundings on gravel, cart paths, and bike trails, and there are prizes for the top three men and women in the half marathon, 10 km, and 5 km, as well as draw prizes based on race numbers. name: Ekeberg Backyard Ultra
description: We are repeating the success from previous years and welcome you to a classic backyard ultra in Oslo's "central park" at Ekeberg. In the midst of the dark and cold time of the year, there is no reason for the running season to come to a halt. Here, you have the chance to run alongside people from the ultrarunner family in delightful surroundings, beautiful nature, with Oslo's skyline and the Oslofjord in the background. Ekeberg Backyard Ultra follows the "Last One Standing" format where the race continues until one runner completes a lap alone, with laps of 6.7 km starting every hour.

name: Frozen Lake Marathon
description: Find your inner Elsa at the Frozen Lake Marathon – an extraordinary running experience. Join an icy adventure on Lake Tisleifjorden in Norway, which is situated 819 meters above sea level. Here, you will have the opportunity to test both endurance and balance on the beautiful, ice-covered Tisleifjorden, where the ice is about 80 cm thick and can support 30 tons. The race consists of one or two 21.1 km laps on a course made of 100% ice, with no inclines, just fantastic views.
course_highlights: Frozen Lake Marathon is the winter's major highlight for running enthusiasts from around the world.
Run on pure ice – no uphill sections, just fantastic views!

Participants can choose between distances from 3 km to half marathon, and there are many experienced pacers to help you find the right pace. description: In brilliant Easter sunshine, 70 runners chose to kick off the Easter holiday by running 42.2 marathon kilometers from Ski to Sandvika. Geir Frykholm, an ultrarunner and head of Løplabbet in Sandvika, has followed up with the Easter Bunny Marathon, where the route goes from Ski to Sandvika. This is a social run with no focus on time, but Øyvind Wang from SkiLøperne became this year's fastest Easter bunny with a time of 3 hours and 17 minutes.

description: This year's Sandtang Relay takes place on Thursday, April 3rd at 6:00 PM in Bryne. It may be beneficial to arrive 45 minutes before the start, as the relay typically lasts for 1 hour and 15 minutes, and it's important to have time to review the course and check the exchange points. The relay features 4 legs for the short course (ages 7-10) and the long course (ages 11 and up), where participants can experience the scenic areas of Gjesdal municipality. The Sandtang Relay is open to everyone, regardless of skill level, and promotes joy in sports and community among participants.
course_highlights: The relay has 4 legs and for the short course (7-10 years): leg 110 m grass + forest floor, leg 100 m forest floor, leg 100 m forest floor, leg 110 m forest floor + gravel + grass.

name: Sjutoppsturen
description: The Seven Peaks Trail is a 15 km long route that traverses five mountains and seven peaks on Sandsøya, offering 1000 meters of elevation gain. The trail is well marked and can be completed year-round, although it is officially organized on Good Friday during Easter. The hike is moderately challenging, and normally fit individuals typically take 4-6 hours to finish. The final section down from Signalen to Hellandsvågane is particularly steep, with sturdy ropes for support.
course_highlights: The course runs over seven mountain peaks on Sandsøya in Sunnmøre.
It is possible to stop after five peaks if you think that is far enough.
The route offers varied terrain, with both uphill and downhill sections, and fantastic views from the peaks.

description: The Easter Marathon in Drammen has gradually become a tradition that marks an early season start for many runners in the Eastern Norway region. Organized for the 11th time by Tom-Rune Bertelsen, this year the race attracted a record number of 170 participants, who enjoyed beautiful spring conditions along the nearly flat course by the Drammenselva. Even though there was some snow and ice in certain parts of the route, the experience was nonetheless fantastic for the participants.
course_highlights: Kenneth Antonsen set a new "personal world record" in the half marathon with a time of 1:41:28.
The winner of the half marathon was Gerhard Sletten from Oslofjord Triathlon, with a time of 2:55:26.
Øystein Mørk from the Lier club SK Kraft won the half distance with a strong time of 1:10:28.

name: Drammen 10K
description: Drammen 10K is a running experience that takes you through a flat and fast course. The race starts at the corner of Drammenshallen and runs along the river, offering a beautiful view. Participants can expect a well-organized event with enthusiasm and support from the crowd. The course, known as one of Europe's fastest, has an elevation gain of 22 meters and provides a pleasant experience regardless of skill level.
course_highlights: The first 1000 meters are very fast and pancake flat.
Over 2000 runners were registered for the first edition, and both the Kenyan world elite and Norwegian runners set personal records.
The finish line is just outside Strømsø Center on Schwartz Street, where participants receive their medals after crossing the finish.

course_highlights: The race is part of the winter series with a total of seven races this season.
There will be three races before Christmas and four after New Year.
Registration for the race starts at 2:20 PM.

name: KRS Ultra
description: It is with great pleasure that we invite you to a fantastic running experience! Join us and explore the beautiful, urban terrain that Kristiansand has to offer. Whether you are an experienced runner with countless ultramarathons behind you, or you are a complete beginner curious about this exciting world, KRSUltra is the perfect way to kick off the season. KRSUltra 60 is a long race in the hills around Kristiansand, featuring a well-marked route that does not require a map or compass.
course_highlights: Participants will have access to drink and food stations along the way, as well as the option for drop bag transport.
A warm meal will be served at the finish line, and it is required to bring your own cup or bottle for drinks.
The maximum time for the race is 12 hours, and it is important to inform the organizer if you need to withdraw from the race.

name: Magni Maraton 99
description: Magni Marathon is a Cannonball-type race, where participants essentially take care of themselves. The race is organized about once a month and was first held on January 10, 2015. Magni Marathon takes place in Trondheim and offers a beautiful route that takes participants through scenic areas, providing a challenging experience for both beginners and experienced runners.
course_highlights: The race is of the Cannonball type, which means that participants are responsible for themselves along the way.
For a half marathon, the participants run 8 laps on a course with the start and finish at Stavset.
Each participant records their own time in the runner's book upon finishing, and the clock is not stopped during the race.

name: Holmestrand Maraton
description: Holmestrand Marathon starts in the city center with a 5 km loop that goes through the northern and southern parts of the town. Participants can choose from several distances, including 5 km, 10 km, half marathon, full marathon, as well as ultrarunning and children's races. The course is fast with few inclines, and many runners will pass through the center several times, creating a lively atmosphere with enthusiastic cheering crowds. When you cross the finish line, a medal, honor, and glory await you, and no matter which distance you choose, you are a winner!
course_highlights: Holmestrand Marathon features a fast course with few uphill sections, ideal for both beginners and experienced runners.
There is a varied offering with distances ranging from a 200-meter kids' race to a marathon, as well as the Daily Double, which combines the marathon distance with a 10 km.
The race promotes public health and motivation, where participants support each other in reaching their goals.

The course winds through scenic areas in Drammen, and the first 1000 meters are very fast and pancake flat. The finish line is just outside Strømsø Senter on Schwartz Gate.

The Spring Run is open to everyone, and you can walk, jog, or run, with options of 5 or 10 km. We encourage everyone to stay in the area until all have crossed the finish line to cheer each other on!

The fastest woman in the 10 km was Esther Innselseth with a time of 41:19.

It attracts both experienced runners and recreational athletes.

description: The Sørlandstest is a low-threshold recreational run for anyone looking for a positive running experience, regardless of ambition level. Whether you are training for a larger goal, want to feel the competition nerves, or just want a social and active day – this is the race for you! You can choose between 5 and 10 km, and all participants receive a medal and a high five. The event focuses on being inclusive and accommodating to all levels of runners, from beginners to experienced.

In 2023, there were 285 completed 5 km races and 159 completed 10 km races, with Andre Åsen (17:21) and Tonja Johansen (19:41) being the fastest in the 5 km, while Bjørn Seter Wastvedt (34:05) and Renate Galleberg (37:42) won the 10 km.

The races take place on Tuesdays with a mass start at 6:00 PM (long) and 6:05 PM (short), along with a children's race at 5:30 PM. name: Sandnes Ultratrail
description: In 2021, the adventure of Sandnes Ultratrail began. The race features distances of 100 miles, 50 miles, 43 km, 23 km, and 10 km, as well as a children's race. The trails wind through beautiful and varied nature, ranging from mountains with stunning fjord views to quiet forest paths, and there are opportunities for swimming in several lovely lakes along the routes. On the longest distance, participants traverse no less than 28 mountains and peaks, and all routes are technically challenging, adding an extra dimension to the experience.
course_highlights: The trails go through beautiful natural landscapes with a mix of technical terrain, forest, and gravel paths.
There are several aid stations along the routes, where experienced volunteers provide nourishment and care.
At the finish line, fantastic Jæder burgers, meat or vegan, are served straight from the grill, and we invite everyone to gather around the bonfire.

The race has been held every year since 2002 and covers a distance of 4.5 kilometers, starting and finishing at Brunstad in Sykkylven. This year, the race took place in Velledalen on May 1, where Kristine Hjellbakk Hole from Sunnylven IL set a new course record in the women's category.
course_highlights: The Konrad Race has been held every year since 2002, covering a distance of 4.5 kilometers with the start and finish at Brunstad in Sykkylven.
Kristine Hjellbakk Hole, Sunnylven IL, set a new course record in the women's category with a time of 16:59, improving her previous record by 44 seconds.

description: The Baksjøløpet was first held in 1981 and is a traditional race that takes place every year in Åbogen in Eidskog. The main course is 11 km, which partly runs on gravel and asphalt roads, while participants who walk without timing can choose an alternative route of 6 km. The event mobilizes about 100 volunteers and attracts over 700 participants, creating a special atmosphere characterized by community spirit and togetherness. Showers and changing rooms are available, and the race is known for its friendly atmosphere and good organization.

The course for the 5 km and 10 km runs along Lille- and Storevatnet, over the bridges by the Coastal Museum to Brendøya (turnaround point for the 5 km), and for those running the SFE-mile, Sørstrand Folk Park with its beautiful view will be part of the route. name: Fløibanen Opp
description: Fløibanen Opp is a spectacular uphill race taking place on April 20, 2026, when the Fløibanen is halted to give you the chance to make your way up to Fløyen along the tracks. This grueling race has a distance of approximately 820 meters with a brutal ascent of 310 meters in elevation, without any variation or breaks. The race offers an intense challenge in the heart of Bergen, and with limited spots available, it is an exclusive opportunity for both experienced runners and beginners looking to test their limits.
course_highlights: On April 20, 2026, the Fløibanen will be stopped for the only time of the year so that YOU can make your way up to Fløyen, along the tracks!
With a distance of approximately 820 meters and an elevation gain of 310 meters, the race offers an intense challenge in the heart of the city.
The audience has access along the entire course, creating an energetic and supportive atmosphere for the participants.

description: The Stomperud Carousel is a running series featuring 4 races that include various distances and laps, including the Bingen Loop at 5 km and the Aasgaard Loop. Shorter races are also organized, such as the 800 m on the track. This provides participants with the opportunity to choose a distance that suits their skill level.
course_highlights: The Stomperud Carousel includes several distances and laps, including the Light Trail, Aasgaard Loop, and Bingen Loop.
Shorter races are also organized, such as the 800 m on the track.

name: Terrengløpskarusell 1
description: The Athletics Group in Oppegård IL is also organizing a cross-country running series this year. The races are open to everyone, regardless of age and ambitions, and will take place on May 6, May 20, June 3, August 26, and September 9 at the Clubhouse, Østre Greverud. Participants can register for 200 NOK for all the races or 80 NOK per individual race. The cross-country races will take place during the training sessions for the athletics group's athletes, and there will be no regular training at Sofiemyr Stadium on the relevant days.
course_highlights: Before the 1st heat begins, there will be group warm-up sessions, where participants will run through the course, ensuring that everyone who is going to race becomes familiar with the layout of the course.

Distribution of race numbers will take place from the stage inside Haraldsvang starting at 5:00 PM, and we ask that the coaches for the groups take responsibility for distributing to their group to avoid congestion.

name: Trønderjogg
description: Trønderjogg 2025 will be held on Tuesday, April 29, starting and finishing at Trondheim Stadium on Øya. The race consists of three events: a 5 km walk at 6:00 PM (from age 6), a 5 km run at 6:30 PM (from age 11), and a 10 km run at 6:45 PM (from age 13). The entry fee is NOK 150 for participants under 18 and NOK 300 for participants aged 18 and older, with an additional fee for a one-time license for those who need it. On the day of the race, registration prices increase by NOK 50 (under 18) or NOK 100 (18 and older).
course_highlights: The race consists of three events: 5 km walking, 5 km, and 10 km.
The entry fee is NOK 150 for participants under 18 years old and NOK 300 for participants 18 years and older.

name: Ålgårdstafetten
description: Gjesdal IL invites you to the Ålgård Relay 2025 on Thursday, April 24. Registration must be completed by April 21, and the entry fee is 200 NOK per team with 4 legs and 300 NOK per team with 6 legs. For participants aged 13 and older, a yearly license or a one-time license purchase is required. The relay has categories for both children and adults, with legs of 1000, 1800, 470, 1400, 470, and 400 meters, and all exchanges take place at the athletics stadium or in the surrounding area.
course_highlights: The Ålgård Relay is a relay race where several people get their very first experience of running a leg at an adult age.
The relay's legs are adapted for both women and men, and the course consists of segments of 1000, 1800, 470, 1400, 470, and 400 meters.
In 2019, over a hundred teams participated, with Sandnes IL fielding 21 teams, and prizes were awarded to all participants up to 10 years old.

name: ASICS Sentrumsløpet
description: ASICS Sentrumsløpet is an annual race in Oslo with distances of 10 km, 5 km, and a children's race. The 10 km race is open to everyone who turns 12 in 2025 and older, while the 5 km race is for those who turn 10 in 2025 and older. The children's race is available for kids who turn 3-11 in 2025. The course for the 10 km starts on Karl Johans gate and includes hilly sections around Frognerparken, as well as an exciting route down towards Oslo City Hall.
course_highlights: The Sentrumsløpet traditionally starts on Karl Johans gate, with a tough uphill stretch towards the Palace.
The course runs in a loop around Frogner Park, where it is gently undulating with opportunities to make up time heading down towards Bygdøy Allé.
Along the way, there are several water stations, as well as lively streets that provide extra motivation for the final kilometers.

name: Røyse Ultra
description: Røyse Ultra is an annual ultramarathon held in Røyse, in the Hole municipality. The race was first organized in 2015, and it takes place in April. Participants run the Hytteplanmila eight times over the course of a day, totaling 80 km. The race consists of 10 kilometers every three hours, making it an ultra interval race.
course_highlights: The race was first held in 2015 and takes place in April.
The race is 8 x 10 km, as they run the Hytteplanmila eight times over the course of a day.
The race consists of running 10 kilometers every three hours, making it an ultra interval race.

name: Fjordkraft Bergen City Marathon
description: Welcome to the Fjordkraft Bergen City Marathon (FBCM) on Saturday, April 25, 2026. This will be the 15th edition of the race, and we look forward to another day filled with the joy of running, community, and urban life at its best. The start and finish line, as usual, will be at Bryggen, where the atmosphere sets the tone for a memorable experience. The course will take you through some of Bergen's most characteristic areas – from Old Bergen and the views along Fjellveien to the new walkway around Store Lungegårdsvann. The Bergen City Marathon 2026 offers a course filled with life, views, and the city's unique atmosphere.
course_highlights: On April 26, 19,000 running enthusiasts gathered to participate in the Fjordkraft Bergen City Marathon.
We are proud to be the main sponsor of a race that focuses on camaraderie, achievement, and inclusion.
The race provides support for a special cause through the event, with support for Downs Syndrome Westland in 2025.

name: Molde Maraton
description: Molde Marathon is an annual running festival in Molde, Møre og Romsdal, bringing together both recreational runners and competitive athletes. The event offers several distances, including a full marathon, half marathon, 10 km, 5 km, and child-friendly races. The race is known for its scenic route along Fannefjorden, featuring spectacular views of the majestic Romsdal Alps. Molde Marathon is held twice a year – as a spring race in April and an autumn race in August.
course_highlights: The event offers several distances, including a full marathon, half marathon, 10 km, 5 km, and child-friendly races.
The race is known for its scenic route along Fannefjorden, with spectacular views of the majestic Romsdal Alps.

description: We at IL Express hope you will come to Fevik Stadium on Saturday, April 27, as we are organizing the half marathon for the 19th time and the Fevik 5 km for the third time! We can offer a certified, fast, and easy-to-run course in a pleasant environment, making it suitable for both experienced runners looking to set a personal best and for first-timers in the half marathon. This is a race for everyone – it doesn't matter how long you expect to take – you are just as welcome regardless!
course_highlights: The half marathon route starts at Fevik Stadium and then continues via Strandsvingen, Moy Moner, Vik, Bringsværd, and further along the old railway line almost to Opplandsvegen.
The 5 km route starts at Fevik stadium at the same time as the half marathon and runs the same way towards Grimstad, before turning at Strand hotel.
The children's race starts at 12:40, and the kids will run one lap on the stadium. Everyone gets a medal.

name: Monolittløpet
description: Welcome spring with a traditional trail run in spectacular surroundings along Iddefjorden in Halden. The Monolith Run is scheduled for April 25, 2026, and has become a tradition for many since the first race was held in 2013. Participants will experience 9 km of challenging yet scenic terrain, starting at the velodrome in Ystehede and finishing at the square in Halden city center. The course features significant elevation and some steep sections, but offers a fantastic nature experience. The race passes through areas where the raw stone for the Vigeland sculpture Monolith was quarried, reminding us of the important stone industry that provided livelihoods for many in the early 20th century.
course_highlights: The Monolith Race has already become a tradition for many, and there is good reason for that.
You can choose whether you want to run, jog, or walk the Monolith Race.
The route of the Monolith Run goes through the areas where the raw stone for the Vigeland sculpture, the Monolith, was quarried.

name: Backyard Ultra
description: Backyard Ultra is a form of ultramarathon where participants complete one lap (typically 4.167 km) every hour for as long as they can. There is no set distance for the race; it continues until only one participant remains. This format creates a unique challenge where both physical endurance and mental strength are crucial.
course_highlights: Participants complete one lap every hour, as long as they can.
There is no set distance for the race; it continues until there is only one participant left.
The format demands both physical endurance and mental strength.

The race has its start and finish area in Gran and Brandbu every other year, and is a collaboration between Gran IL, Brandbu IF, Gran Shopping Center, and Brandbu Shopping Center. The Viggaløpet marks its 30th year, and although the traditional race was canceled, participants are encouraged to continue running.

Bring your friends, gather your colleagues, or form a team with strangers – the most important thing is to have fun! Starting and finishing at the square in Halden, the 10 legs run along the fjord and around Hovsfjellet in beautiful nature. Each leg has varying lengths, elevation, and difficulty levels, making the race accessible to everyone.

Ivar Skåre is personally responsible for Espe Rundt, and the start line is at his garage door in Birkeland. This year, 104 participants took part in the run around the lake.

description: VOM DOGRUN is a pleasant activity for everyone who wants to be active together with their dog. Participants can choose to participate with or without timing, and the event is a social activity for the whole family. The start and finish are at the (old) Dog Meadow in Frogner Park, where participants can choose between two classes: Dogrun, which is a 7 km race with timing (two laps), and Dogwalk, which is a 3.5 km walk without timing.

name: Aron Opp
description: We are excited to present the fall's most intense challenge - Aron Opp! This is a hill climb race organized by Bedriftsidretten Buskerud and Vestfold in collaboration with Skimore Drammen and Arontunet Lodge. The start takes place at the bottom of the ski slope and follows the road in a loop up to the top, where the finish line is at the lift house. The course is approximately 1.7 km, where the fastest runners take about 10 minutes, and it takes 30-45 minutes at a brisk walk. New this year is the relay, which will be conducted in stages with a total of 5 legs of 350 meters each.
course_highlights: The course follows the gravel road in a loop along the ski slope from the bottom to the top.

name: Terrengløpskarusellen løp
description: The Cross-Country Running Carousel Race 1 is part of a series of three races organized by Haugesund Idrettslag. The courses mostly run on gravel paths, but there is some terrain with forest cover (approximately 200m per lap on the 620m courses). The start and finish for all courses are at the stage/pavilion inside Haraldsvang, and there will be an awards ceremony after the final race from the stage in Haraldsvang.

name: Namdalskarusellen løp 2
description: The Namdal Carousel 2025 consists of several races, including cross-country running on Otterøya, 800 m at Kleppen, 3000 m at Svenningmoen, 5 km at Hestmarka, a 3 km road race, and Klompen uphill. The carousel has two participant classes: participation with timing and participation without timing. There is also a distance called Namdalsmila. Welcome to an exciting carousel in Namsos!
course_highlights: This year's Namdalskarusell follows somewhat of the same recipe as in 2024.
The following race is included in this year's series: 800 m at Kleppen (April 29, 2025).

name: Sørdalskarusellen Kringsjåløpet
description: The Kringsjåløpet is 2.71 km long and starts and finishes at Nordre Ål school. The start is on Gamle Kringsjåvei on the bridge over Skurva right by Nordre Ål school, and the route follows Kringsjåveien northward, takes the footpath down to Ekromskogen, goes through the upper section southward, and follows Teigveien back to Nordre Ål school. The race is being organized for the 43rd time in 2024, featuring both a mass start and a virtual race. The results will be sent to Kondis.no for statistical recording.
course_highlights: There will be a virtual race from Saturday to Tuesday and a mass start on Wednesday, April 24th at 7:00 PM.
Hoka will have a booth in the start area with great offers, and Sport 1 is sponsoring sports drinks for all participants at the finish line.
The course is officially measured at 3 km, but this year it is 70 meters shorter than last year.

name: Søndagsløpet Sarpsborg
description: The Sunday Run is a popular race that takes place in Kalnesskogen in the municipality of Sarpsborg, and was started in 2014. The race is held every Sunday from April to mid-October, featuring three courses of varying lengths: the yellow at 7.05 km, the green at 8.87 km, and the red at 10.2 km. The courses vary in difficulty, with the red course having steep climbs, especially between 5 and 6 km. The Sunday Run is free to participate in and is suitable for all levels, from recreational runners to elite athletes.
course_highlights: The race has three different courses: yellow, green, and red, each offering unique challenges for various levels of runners.
Participants can expect well-organized conditions, with opportunities to set personal records and compete against others.
The Sunday race is free to participate in and has been a part of the running community in Sarpsborg for many years.

This is a green route in Eide, with a length of 5.06 km and an elevation gain of 52 m, which takes about 1 hour and 25 minutes to complete. The event has been held annually since 2019, usually on May 1st.
course_highlights: The route goes over the Holmsund Bridge, past Svanviken and in by or along the Vågsbø River.

name: mailøpet
description: We welcome you to the mail race on May 11 and the junior festival on May 12, where both races start at 8:00 AM. The 58th mail race had great running weather and good conditions for both runners and spectators, with a total of 141 participants, including 38 in junior, senior, and veteran classes. The men's winner was Vetle Uhre Hammersvik from Førde with a time of 9:55, while the women's winner was Eli Karin Sjåstad Åsebø from Volda with a time of 14:08.
course_highlights: It was the young man Vetle Uhre Hammersvik from Førde, but with close roots from Selje, who decided the 1st mail race of 2016 in a fierce duel against last year's champion Eirik Voksøy Bringvor from Sandsøy, winning by just one second.
We welcome you to the mail race on May 11 and the junior festival on May 12. Entrance is 150,- per day or 200,- for the whole weekend. Children under 12 get in for free.
The men's winner this year, as last year, was Vetle Uhre Hammersvik from Førde with a strong time of 9:55. The women's winner was Eli Karin Sjåstad Åsebø from Volda with 14:08.

name: Strandamilå
description: Strandamilå 2023 was held for the 43rd time and was finally back as a family race! Despite less than favorable weather conditions, there was an impressive turnout with over 550 participants across all distances, and the registration nearly matched the best numbers of the last 15 years with 125 sign-ups. The Girls' Run is a low-threshold race that promises an unforgettable running celebration for women, having gathered up to 12,000 participants, which creates a festive atmosphere and engagement in the local community.

name: Skogvokteren Ultra
description: Welcome to the fourth edition of the Skogvokteren Ultra! This is a low-threshold, unmarked race with 100% trail magic, where we gather in the forests of Grenland to celebrate spring and compete for honor and glory. Skogvokting is about appreciating the local environment, community, and celebrating the ability to move efficiently through the terrain. We hope to see you sharp and ready at five o'clock on Saturday, May 4, 2024, when the race kicks off in Porsgrunn.
course_highlights: The Skogvokteren Ultra is Grenland's annual ultra celebration with a low-threshold and authentic profile on spring trails during the transition from April to May.
The race is a UTMB Index event at 100K with a distance of 88.00 km and an elevation gain of 3700 meters.
We focus on mastery and progression, but we also facilitate performance.

description: On Tuesday, the famous beach race took place in Etape Bornholm, which is quite unique in its kind. It is the shortest of the stage races, only 5.8 kilometers long, but also the most difficult and challenging for many. 4 of the kilometers are on sandy beach along the water's edge or in loose sand dunes, much like in a desert. Either you really like this very special race, or you hate it.
course_highlights: Norwegian Vikings, however, mastered the unusual terrain very well.

description: Wings for Life World Run is a unique race where participants run for a good cause. The participants must run as far as they can before being "caught" by the car. The race takes place simultaneously in many locations around the world, and the proceeds go to research on spinal cord injuries.

The race offers several distances for participants, including 600 meters for the youngest and longer distances for adults. The courses run through scenic areas, making it a great opportunity to experience the beautiful nature around Ilseng.

name: Krystallmarsjen
description: The Crystal March is a collaboration with Magnor Glassworks and was first held in 1982. The race takes place every spring, starting and finishing at Magnor Glassworks, and is open to both active runners, joggers, and walkers. There are courses of 8.5 km and 5 km available, as well as a junior march of 2.5 km for the youngest participants. Everyone who finishes receives a crystal plate from Magnor Glassworks, and there are prizes in each category.

name: Fevik Løbestævne
description: Fevik Running Event is a popular race event that takes place at Fevik Stadium, where everyone is welcome to participate in the distances of 3,000, 5,000, and 10,000 meters. The event is known for attracting participants from various levels and provides a great opportunity for both beginners and experienced runners to compete. The race will be held on Sunday, October 12th, and registration is free. Participants can expect a well-organized and exciting experience.

name: Wings For Life Run
description: Wings for Life World Run is a unique race where participants run to support research on spinal cord injuries. The race does not have a fixed distance; instead, participants run as far as they can before being caught by a "Catcher Car." This creates an exciting and dynamic experience, as all participants start at the same time, but the goal is to run as far as possible before the car catches up with them. 100% of the entry fee goes directly to the Wings for Life Foundation to fund research.
course_highlights: Participants can choose their own distance, whether they run or roll in a wheelchair.
The race brings together thousands of participants from around the world who compete simultaneously.
Participants can register via the app, which has features like GPS tracking and a virtual Catcher Car.

name: Kanada Rundt
description: Kanada Rundt is an annual street race in Sylling, held since 1981. On Tuesday, May 13, 2025, the race will take place for the 43rd time, where runners can choose between distances of 6 or 12 km. Participants in the fitness class can decide whether to walk or run, without timing. The 12 km street race follows the classic route around Kanada, while the 6 km race follows the main course to the Kyllerud roundabout before returning to Syllinghallen.
course_highlights: Participants will experience the beautiful nature around Sylling while competing in a friendly atmosphere.
The race has been a part of the running community for over 30 years and attracts both experienced runners and beginners.

The race covers a distance of 4.6 km and is suitable for both experienced runners and beginners, with a non-timed fun run starting at 11:00 AM, a children's race at 11:30 AM, and competitive classes at 12:00 PM. Participants can compete in several age categories, and there will be prizes for class winners as well as draw prizes.

The route follows the gravel path along the Namsen and includes varied surfaces such as gravel road, asphalt, and a bit of trail.

description: Welcome to Storehaugen Opp! This race takes place on Ascension Day 2026, offering participants the chance to experience a challenging uphill run in beautiful surroundings. The course is designed to test endurance and strength, featuring a route up Storehaugen that provides fantastic views over Lærdal and the surrounding area. Participants will experience varied terrain with both trails and gravel roads, offering an authentic nature experience.

name: Ekebergløpet Stafett
description: Join us for the most beautiful spring fun run in scenic surroundings around Ekebergsletta! The Ekeberg Run 2025 will be held on Sunday, May 25, and is a race for everyone, regardless of age and level. Whether you are an experienced runner or a beginner, this is a fantastic opportunity to challenge yourself and experience the community in a race that brings the whole local community together. The Ekeberg Run is a perfect chance to push your limits and enjoy the beautiful nature at Ekebergsletta.
course_highlights: The recreational race follows the national classification system for adults and has a long tradition at Ekebergsletta.

description: The Land Relay is a relay race for age groups 11 to 16 years, taking place in Søndre Land. The relay was reorganized in 2013 and consists of 8 legs for both genders, where each team's eight runners cannot exceed a total age of 108 years. Younger runners than 11 years can participate but will be counted as 11 years in the relay. All legs can be viewed from the spectator area northwest of the town hall, and the race has its start and finish at Hovsbakken, right behind the town hall.

Participants receive a beautiful mug as a prize, and the course takes place in scenic surroundings around Tjomsevannet, with the start and finish at Søgne Old Rectory.

Søndre Land IL Athletics and Søndre Land IL Ski are collaborating on this event, which has brought together both recreational runners and professional uphill racers since its inception. The race features a 400-meter elevation gain over 4000 meters from the boat harbor in Kråkvika up to Helvetestoppen. Runners pass through Hov center on their way up, and there are great opportunities to follow the runners from the spectator area. The race starts at 12:00 PM, and it is possible to register for both the timed running category and the non-timed recreational class.

The course starts outside the clubhouse and goes up the hill to the right of the garage, then follows a marked trail up to the Skifjell mountain area.

name: Eikenosa Opp
description: Eikenosa Opp is a mountain race in Ålesund organized by Emblem IL. The race was first held in 2004 and starts at about 2 meters above sea level at the bottom of Eikenosvågen, 18 km east of Ålesund city center. The course is 4.5 km long and runs on asphalt and gravel roads, finishing at the west end of the dam at Røssevollsvatnet at 295 meters. The men's course record is 17 minutes and 55 seconds, set by Johan Bugge in 2019, while the women's record is 22 minutes and 3 seconds by Ingrid Festøs from 2017.
course_highlights: The course has an elevation gain of approximately 300 meters.
The race finishes at Røssevollvatnet, which is located 295 meters above sea level.
The distribution of race numbers takes place at KIWI Flisnes, and parking can be done at the stores in Flisnes.

The island is a popular spot for running, with varied terrain and countless picture-perfect viewpoints, providing a perfect foundation for a fun and memorable course, whether you're running for the first time or competing at the front of the elite class.

Modum FIK participated with 4 teams, with the girls taking home the trophy for the second year in a row, while the boys were defeated by Sigdal 1 and 2. This uphill race in Oslo is filled with running enthusiasts, fast legs, and great energy. The course starts at Muselunden by Sinsenkrysset at an elevation of 110 meters and ascends to the top of Grefsenkollen at 380 meters above sea level, with a total distance of 4.5 km. This race offers an unforgettable journey through some of the most scenic landscapes on this side of Eastern Norway, featuring a mix of runnable coastal trails, rocky beaches, winding roots, beautiful pine forests, charming towns, dense woods, and stunning views. Endless Shore Ultra offers distances of 50 and 100 miles and is open for registration for both novice and experienced runners.

name: Hamarløpet
description: Hamarløpet is a 10-kilometer street race through the beautiful surroundings of the inland town of Hamar. The purpose of Hamarløpet is to contribute to public health by motivating both young and old to lead active lives. The race aims to be an arena for both the fastest runners and those who typically do not participate in other racing events, encouraging a joy of activity without prestige. Organized by the Hamarløpet Association, this is an ideal initiative where any profits go to charitable causes.
course_highlights: The course for the Hamarløpet is a flat and officially measured 10-kilometer route that runs along beautiful paths by Lake Mjøsa, starting from Hamar city center.
The start and finish line are at Skibladnerbrygga, and the race goes through Koigen, Domkirkeodden, Strandveien, and the two railway underpasses.
There will be a water station and split time at 5 km, and the race will take place on Saturday, May 23 at 1:00 PM.

In addition to the main races, there is also a children's race of 500 m, making this a family-friendly celebration for all running enthusiasts.

It is an excellent opportunity to set a new personal record.
course_highlights: Our course is definitely one of the fastest in the country, and it doesn't hurt that it's also spectacular – as it runs along the promenade by the fjord.
Almost 500 runners were registered for the 5 and 10 km events at Strindheim's Nidaros Running Festival at Skansen in Trondheim.
The routes run along the lake towards Brattøra, turn around, and make a loop out to Ila before leading to a nice final stretch along the silos to the finish line.

name: Oslo Løpsfestival
description: Oslo Running Festival consists of eight races along the capital's beautiful trails and scenic roads. You can run whenever you want – alone or with others. You can participate individually in the SOLO category, or in the team competition as a DUO or TRIO. In DUO and TRIO, you can compete in the women's, men's, and mixed categories. Each race is announced on a Friday at 12:00, and the course is open until Sunday at 11:00 the following weekend.
course_highlights: Oslo Running Festival offers both individual and team competitions.
The routes run along beautiful trails and roads in Oslo.
The race has an opening period of just over a week to complete the distance.

name: Perseløpet 5 & 10 km
description: The Perseløpet 5 & 10 km is an exciting running event set in picturesque surroundings. The courses are designed to provide both beginners and experienced runners with a challenging yet rewarding experience. Participants can choose between two distances: 5 km and 10 km, both offering a fast and flat AIMS-certified course designed for records. There is a strong emphasis on community and the joy of running, with results available immediately after finishing and free parking.
course_highlights: Fast and flat course, designed for records. AIMS-certified course.
Results available immediately after finishing.
Free parking.

name: Rundt Torghatten
description: TORGHATTEN RUNDT is part of the "Race Carousel" and takes place every year on the second day of Pentecost. Distance: From the community house at Torget, around the legendary Torghatten, and back to the community house. The surface consists of asphalt, gravel, and natural terrain, making the race accessible for all categories.
course_highlights: The race takes place every year on the second day of Pentecost.
Distance: From the community house at the square, around the legendary Torghatten, and back to the community house.
The surface is asphalt, gravel, and natural terrain.

name: Kleivane Rundt
description: Kleivane Rundt is a local recreational and competitive race that takes place every year on the second day of Pentecost in Stette, Sunnmøre, and has been organized since 1985 by Stettevik Sports Club. The race includes a fun class/family class before the competitive runners tackle the course, and the entire village actively participates in the event. The route spans nearly 10 km with about 170 positive elevation meters, offering a varied course with asphalt, gravel, forest road, and technical trail in a beautiful landscape with views of mountains and fjords. After the race, there is social gathering with food and a raffle for prizes.
course_highlights: The race features a varied route with asphalt, gravel, forest roads, and a small section of technical trail, all set in a beautiful Sunnmøre landscape.
There is a recreational class/family class that runs the course before the competing runners, and the whole village participates in the event.
The course is tough with several uphill sections, especially the one over Kleiva, but offers plenty of downhill towards the finish.

name: Saldilten
description: Saldilten is a road race that takes place along the gravel road by the beautiful Heimdalsbotnet in Vemundvik, Namsos municipality. The race, now in its 34th year, is typically held on the second day of Pentecost each year and has been designated a quality race by the Norwegian Organization for Endurance Sports – Kondis, which means that the courses are officially measured. Competition classes are offered from the 12-13 age group, allowing young people to participate in healthy competition.
course_highlights: The race has been designated as a quality race by the Norwegian Organization for Endurance Sports – Kondis, which means that the courses are officially measured.
The race has competition classes for the 12-13 age group, allowing eager young runners to challenge their peers in healthy competition.
The Saldilten is normally held on the second day of Pentecost each year and runs along the beautiful Heimdalsbotnet.

description: Welcome to TUIL – the carousel, a running festival for children and youth! TUIL Athletics (“TUIL Running”) is repeating its success and is delighted to invite you to the TUIL carousel – for children and youth! We are organizing 7 races in Tromsdalen for children and youth, where you can choose the distance and whether you want timing. The optional distances are 650m and 1850m, with a registration fee of NOK 250 for all 7 races. Included in the registration fee are a participant t-shirt, a participation medal, and nice prizes that will be drawn at the last race.
course_highlights: We are organizing 7 races in Tromsdalen for children and youth, you can choose the distance and whether you want timing.

name: OBOS Fornebuløpet
description: The OBOS Fornebuløpet is perhaps Norway's largest midweek race, taking place on May 21 in Fornebu. The 5 km course starts at UNITY Arena, goes past the Equinor building along the water before turning into Nansenparken. The entire route is on asphalt, primarily on walking/cycling paths, and there will be a water station at Storøya School after about 3.4 km and at the finish line. Participants will have their own area in UNITY Arena for changing clothes and for food/drink between distances.
course_highlights: The course runs on asphalt, primarily a pedestrian/bicycle path.
There is a water station at Storøya School after about 3.4 km and at the finish line.
Participants will have their own area in the UNITY Arena for changing clothes and food/drinks between the distances.

name: Land Løpskarusell
description: The Land Running Carousel is an annual running series that takes place from May to September, featuring 11 events in Søndre and Nordre Land. The races include cross-country running at distances of 400m, 1800m, and 3600m, as well as track events with distances of 300m, 600m, and 1500m. It is a great opportunity for both experienced runners and beginners to participate in varied races and enjoy the beautiful nature of the area.
course_highlights: RACE 1: Wednesday, April 30 at 6:30 PM: Lyngstrand Camping. Cross-country run 400, 1800, and 3600 m.
RACE 2: Wednesday, May 7 at 6:30 PM: Dokka Stadium. Track events 300m, 600m, and 1500m, combined events with 60m, long jump, and small ball for children.
3rd race in the Land Carousel: 3.2 km trail run at the Land Museum.

description: We are excited to welcome you to the 18th edition of the Helse Førde Relay. Experience the great atmosphere at the start and finish at the hospital in Førde, and join the fun run, the rocket course, one of the children's races, or a team in the relay. The main course consists of 6 legs and is 5.5 kilometers long, and there will also be children's races and a variety of activities for the audience. The relay starts at 6:30 PM, and everyone can participate, either as runners or supporters.
course_highlights: The main course consists of 6 stages and is 5.5 kilometers long, which includes various surfaces such as asphalt and gravel.
There was a strong turnout and beautiful weather for running, with many participating in costumes and children's races as part of the event.

name: Arctic Triple Ultratrail
description: Arctic Triple // Lofoten Ultra-Trail® is a trail race that takes you through the spectacular Lofoten Islands from Moskenesøy to Austvågøy. The race takes place in week 22 each year, and the routes pass through amazing landscapes of mountain ridges, white beaches, green hills, and gray cliffs, with the sea always in sight. The finish line is in the picturesque town of Svolvær, surrounded by steep mountains by the harbor – pure magic.
course_highlights: Lofoten Ultra-Trail was mentioned in Runners World (Oct. 2017) as one of the most beautiful races in the world and consists of several different distances.
The extreme distance is 100 miles (166 km) and starts at the innermost part of the spectacular Kjerkfjorden, near Reine in western Lofoten.

The popular distance of the Lofoten Ultra-Trail is 24 km and crosses 2 mountains with a total elevation gain of 1000 meters, offering a fantastic 360-degree panoramic view of Lofoten's beautiful mountains and sea.

description: Tomorrow, September 5th, the final race of this year's Fun Run Series will take place. We conclude where we started – SKOLERUTA! We hope as many as possible, young and old, will join us for the last race of the series this year. You can walk, jog, or run – it's entirely up to you, with or without timing. Welcome!
course_highlights: There was a FANTASTIC turnout at the first race, with both young and old gathering at the starting line under a brilliant blue sky and sun.
The joy of running at a high level characterized the event, and we had some lucky winners of our draw prizes.

name: Festaløpet
description: The Festal Race is a content-rich and varied event taking place on Saturday, May 24, 2025, at 1:00 PM at Ålbusøyvegen 226, 7340 Oppdal, Norway. The course takes you through the old power station, further into the forest, along dramatic cliffs, past waterfalls, and up into open mountain terrain. Towards the end, a long flow trail awaits, leading you back to the finish inside the impressive machine room. This race is a great opportunity for both experienced runners and beginners to participate in an exciting and challenging atmosphere.
course_highlights: The course takes you through the old power station, further into the forest, along dramatic ravines, past waterfalls, and up into open mountain terrain.
Towards the end, a long flow path awaits that leads you back to the finish line inside the powerful engine room.
This race is a great opportunity for both experienced runners and beginners to participate in an exciting and challenging atmosphere.

name: Ulriken Opp
description: Ulriken Opp 2026 takes place on Saturday, May 30, and is a hill climb race that goes from the lower station to the upper station on Ulriken, the highest of the 7 mountains surrounding Bergen. The course has an elevation difference of about 405 meters from the starting area at 200 meters above sea level to the summit at 605 meters above sea level, and the distance is measured at approximately 1730 meters for the TRIM and MOSJON classes, while the COMPETITION CLASS has a distance of 3.6 km. The course offers varied terrain, from gravel to steep stairs, and provides a spectacular view of Bergen and the North Sea.
course_highlights: Ulriken Opp consists of 3 different trails; “Grieg Oppstemten Uphill”, “Drevelin Montana Classic”, and Cani Cross (handler with dog).
The start is from Montana (the gravel track) and the finish is at the top of Ulriken at 605 meters above sea level.
There are recorded course records for both men and women in the competitive class.

name: Sømnamile
description: Welcome to a measured and fast mile along our beautiful coast in the far south of Helgeland! The event is organized by Sømna Sports Club in collaboration with Sparebank 1 Helgeland and HEV. We hope that YOU will come, regardless of your level, as there is room for both the competitive runner who wants to race against the clock and the recreational runner who just wants to finish. The start and finish line is at the athletics stadium in the municipal center of Vik, and you can choose between 10 km and 5 km with or without timing. Runners under 10 years old can participate in the children's race of 600 meters around the stadium.
course_highlights: Sømnamile - Norway's most beautiful mile!
The start and finish are at the athletics stadium in the municipal center of Vik.

name: Farsund Maraton
description: Farsund Marathon is one of Norway's most beautiful races, taking place through a spectacular natural and cultural landscape. The marathon is held in Farsund and offers various distances, including full marathon, half marathon, children's marathon, and relays. In 2025, the race gathered 985 participants, and the weather was ideal with a light breeze and full sun, contributing to a positive experience for everyone.

The marathon runners were given the opportunity for an early start on the marathon distance, starting one hour before the main race.

name: Glommaløpet
description: In the Glommaløpet, you run on a gravel path along the last kilometer of the Glomma River from Sarpefossen to the river's mouth at the sea near Gamlebyen in Fredrikstad. The race starts at the square in Sarpsborg, and the route goes through Kulåsparken, over Sannesundsbrua, along the Glommastien (the eastern side of the Glomma), under the Fredrikstad Bridge, finishing in the best-preserved fortress town in the Nordics – Gamlebyen. The race takes place on May 30, 2026, and offers several distances, including a relay for teams of up to ten participants and an individual 10-mile race.
course_highlights: The Glommaløpet offers beautiful nature experiences along the Glomma River and is open to everyone, regardless of level.
The course is flat and easy to run, with water stations at 4.5, 9.5, and 14.5 km.
A portion of the profits goes to the Cancer Society.

name: Ecotrail Oslo

The courses take you through beautiful nature with elevation gains that vary depending on the distance, providing a unique opportunity to experience Oslo's scenic beauty. The tenth edition of Ecotrail Oslo will be held on May 24, 2025, and this is a race for all age groups and levels.
course_highlights: The course runs on urban trails and technical paths through Nordmarka and Bærumsmarka.
The last five kilometers are on asphalt along the fjord and into the shared finish line at Vippa.

The course follows a safe walking and cycling path and is suitable for all age groups; big and small, young and old. Here you can roll, walk, jog, or run, and it’s a perfect opportunity to set a personal record or complete your first fun run.
course_highlights: The race takes place around Store Lungegårdsvannet in Bergen, covering a distance of 3000 meters (3 KM).
The course route follows a safe walking and cycling path all the way around the lake, and is suitable for all age groups.
There is no requirement to run; you can roll, walk, jog, or run.

The Summer Run marks a fitting conclusion to the project, but it is just a comma in this group's running and podcasting journey.

name: Trondheimstafetten
description: The Trondheim Relay is public health at its best, movement in a fantastic setting. On May 30, 2026, the Trondheim Relay will be held for the first time, starting at Skansen and featuring a route that goes from park to park, ending at Trondheim Stadium. The relay consists of 10 stages and 20 runner-friendly kilometers along new walking and cycling paths, allowing participants to experience the city's culture and history. The Trondheim Relay is suitable for all ages and levels, and is a great sporting event that promotes community and activity.
course_highlights: The first leg of the Trondheim relay is 1609 meters and runs through the city's new "dream mile."
Each stage has its own character, ranging from flat and fast stretches to more hilly and technically challenging sections.
The Trondheim Relay is suitable for all ages and levels, and encourages team formation in workplaces, associations, residential communities, friend groups, or families.

name: Minneløpet
description: Captain Dreyer's Memorial Race is a running competition that offers distances for all age groups, including a 12 km course for active participants and a 1 km children's race without timing. The race takes place at Hydro Aluminium Sunndal, with a start time of 10:00 for the non-timed category and 13:00 for the active classes. There are prizes for the best times in each class, as well as cash prizes for the top three women and men.
course_highlights: The race offers a 12 km course for active participants and a 1 km children's run without timing.
There are prizes for the best times in each category, as well as cash prizes for the top three women and men.
The race is organized at Hydro Aluminium Sunndal, with a start time of 10:00 AM for the recreational class and 1:00 PM for the competitive classes.

name: Oppdalskarusellen 2. løp
description: The second race in the Oppdal Carousel 2025 was held on Sunday, May 25, at 2:00 PM from the NOIL area in windy and wet weather. Despite the conditions, many runners lined up at the start for the 3.18 km course with an elevation gain of 47 meters. In the women's category, Bente Lien Hæhre from NOIL took the victory with a time of 13:35.5, just under six seconds ahead of Solveig Egge Greftegreff from Brandbu IF. In the men's category, Mads Berge from NOIL was the fastest to finish with a time of 10:26.8.
course_highlights: Bente Lien Hæhre from NOIL won the women's class with a time of 13:35.5.
Mads Berge from NOIL was the fastest in the men's class with a time of 10:26.8.
The course was 3.18 km long with an elevation gain of 47 meters.

name: Skaubygdaløpet
description: Skaubygdaløpet is a tough half marathon in somewhat very hilly terrain on Nesodden, organized on hiking trails in Nordre Frogn. The race distances with timing are 21.1 km and 7.1 km, with a separate category "Open Course" at 3.7 or 6.4 km without timing. The courses have a challenging profile, where one does not set personal records, but must calculate their own pace and finish with style. For the children, there are 200m and 600m races.
course_highlights: Course lengths with timing are 21.1 km and 7.1 km.
We also have a separate category "Open Course" at 3.7 or 6.4 km without timing.
For the children, we are organizing 200m and 600m races.

name: Straumemila
description: The Straumemila running festival offers several distances for runners of all ages and skill levels, including 10 km, 5 km, and the Children's Mile. The race takes place in scenic surroundings and has a friendly atmosphere that promotes community and enjoyment for all participants. There are also prizes for the best performances and opportunities to set new course records. Organized by Sotra Sports Club, Straumemila aims to facilitate increased activity in the region through play, competition, and community.
course_highlights: The race takes place in scenic surroundings and has a friendly atmosphere that promotes community and joy for all participants.
There are also prizes for the best performances and opportunities to set new course records.
The Straumemila consists of a total of seven different races or events, making it possible for everyone to find a race or event that suits them.

name: Vettisløpet
description: The Vettisløpet in Øvre Årdal is not only beautiful, with the stunning Hjellefossen, Avdalsfossen, and Vettisfossen providing a magical and lovely backdrop. It is also a tough race with many steep hills over 9 km. The traditional Vettisløpet takes place in Utladalen on Sunday, May 25, 2025, with the option to register in both recreational and active categories.
course_highlights: The Vettisløpet is a tough race with many steep hills over 9 km.
The race has a fantastic backdrop with Hjellefossen, Avdalsfossen, and Vettisfossen.
It is possible to register for both the recreational and competitive classes.

name: Arctic Triple Ultratrail
description: The Arctic Triple // Lofoten Ultra-Trail® is a trail run that takes you through the stunning archipelago from Moskenesøy to Austvågøy. The race takes place in week 22 each year and offers spectacular nature with mountain ridges, white beaches, green hills, and gray cliffs, where the sea is always in sight. The finish line is in the beautiful town of Svolvær, surrounded by steep mountains by the harbor. This race is described as one of the most beautiful in the world.
course_highlights: The extreme distance is 100 miles (166 km) and starts at the innermost part of the spectacular Kjerkfjorden, near Reine in western Lofoten.
The course winds its way through large parts of the archipelago, over mountains, ridges, and beaches before finishing at Svolvær Square.
The mountains offer a fantastic 360-degree panoramic view of the beautiful mountains and sea of the Lofoten Islands.

The course is incredibly fast and easy to run, and both the marathon and half marathon will converge at the entrance to Myrvegen, where there will be a merging area of over 1 km to ensure ample space for all participants. Come and try our renowned course, and kick off the summer with a quality race!
course_highlights: Jessheim Half Marathon and 5 km, an incredibly fast and easy-to-run course in Jessheim.
The marathon and half marathon will meet at the entrance to Myrvegen.
Choose between a half marathon, 5 km, or a super cool kids' race.

Both routes have a challenging ascent towards the end, and timing is carried out using RFID technology.
course_highlights: The Risør Race has two distances - 5 and 10 km - in addition to a children's race (free).
The 10 km course runs through beautiful hiking terrain in Åmlandskauen, up to Kvernsmyr and Vemmelstjenn.
Both courses have an incline towards the end.

Participants can look forward to a scenic route that takes them through stunning landscapes, featuring both fjords and mountains. The course is designed to be challenging but also accessible to runners of all levels.

name: Steinkjermila
description: Join the fun run and community festival Steinkjermila, suitable for the whole family. Here you can participate in the Mila, the 5K, or the 5K walking group for those who prefer to walk. Steinkjermila was held for the first time in 2021 and has since become a fantastic event in the heart of Steinkjer city center. The start and finish are at Steinkjer square, and the Steinkjermila course winds through many of the city's most beautiful spots, including Rismelen activity park and the lovely promenade along the lake. Mark your calendar and bring the whole family to this spring's great community celebration in Steinkjer city center.
course_highlights: The start and finish are at Steinkjer square, and the Steinkjer marathon route winds through many of the city's most beautiful spots.
Participants will run through the Rismelen Activity Park, along the Steinkjer River on both sides, and past the Health and Emergency Preparedness House.
The course also takes a detour to the city beach before crossing the Steinkjer Bridge where the audience cheers the participants on.

name: Jentebølgen Ålesund
description: This year, Jentebølgen Ålesund will be held on Thursday, September 19, at Sparebanken Møre Arena. Bring your good friends, colleagues, or family, and join the most enjoyable running celebration of the year! Jentebølgen is a public health run of just under 5 km specifically aimed at women, with the goal of promoting physical activity, mental health, and community. The event kicks off with entertainment at 6:15 PM, and the starting signal will be given at 7:00 PM after a group warm-up together with Stamina Trening.
course_highlights: The Girls' Wave in Ålesund is organized by IL Valder for the 16th time in 2024, and is open to everyone.
With around 800 active women last year, Jentebølgen was the largest fitness race in Møre og Romsdal - and also the healthiest.
NOK 10 per runner is donated to Mental Helse Ungdom to give young people a reason to choose life.

name: Rotvollfjæra Frontyard
description: Rotvollfjæra Frontyard Ultra is a different and shorter variant than Backyard, where the combination of speed and endurance becomes more significant as the race progresses. Participants have 30 minutes to complete the first lap, with time limits reduced by one minute for each subsequent lap. From the 19th lap, runners must cover 3 km within 12 minutes, which corresponds to an average speed of 15 km/h. The race lasts until the 27th lap, where one could potentially have run 50 miles (almost 2 marathons).
course_highlights: You have 30 minutes to complete the first lap, and most people manage this.
If you miss the deadline, you are out of the race.
From the 19th lap onwards, the time limit will remain the same until the race concludes after the 27th lap.

course_highlights: Participants will experience beautiful natural scenery in Risør.
The course includes varied terrain, from forest trails to open landscapes.
There are several distances available, tailored for both beginners and experienced runners.

name: Elverumtrimmen - løp
description: Elverumtrimmen is a running series that has become part of my regular routine, and I have tested myself on the course the last two Mondays. There is a steady positive development, even though my time on the 5.3 km isn't impressive. I have over 170 test runs on this course since it was opened in 2000, and the course started on asphalt before transitioning to more challenging terrain with rocks. There was a new record and nearly 100 active participants gathered and ready to start, and the weather was ideal.
course_highlights: Elverumtrimmen is a running carousel for everyone, regardless of age, pace, and level, on Mondays.
The course has been in use since 2000, and I have found that it's faster to run with a steady pace instead of walking.

The race attracted participants from all over the country and offers a beautiful course through the stunning surroundings of Holtålen municipality. It is known for its friendly atmosphere and varied race distances, which include children's races, a recreational class (2.5 km or 5 km), and the main race (5 km or 10 km). Gauldalsløpet is an important gathering place for runners of all ages, with a focus on community, joy of sport, and physical activity.

name: Jentebølgen - Trondheim & Molde
description: Jentebølgen is a public health run of 5-6 km, specifically aimed at women, with the goal of promoting physical activity, mental health, and community. This informal race, which takes place on June 2nd, encourages girls of all ages to participate, regardless of fitness level. Last year, nearly 17,000 girls took part, and this year the organizer hopes for 20,000. The main partner is Mental Helse Ungdom, which works to give young people a reason to choose life.
course_highlights: Jentebølgen is about experiencing mastery, having fun, and encouraging women and girls to be active.

There is no age limit for the non-timed run, and the age limit is 13 years for the timed run. The race is organized on June 11, 2025.

Berit Mogstad set a new course record with a time of 6:22, while Magnus Øyen also achieved a personal best. With 29 participants in the club championship, it remains a popular event, even though the number of participants was lower than usual.
course_highlights: Berit Mogstad set a new course record with a time of 6:22, and Magnus Øyen achieved a personal best with 6:20.
The course is considered easy to run, with nice trail sections and good gravel roads, and has mostly remained the same since its inception in 1974.
There were 29 participants in the club championship, despite the bad weather before the race, which is believed to have affected attendance.

The course stretches across 2 counties and 5 municipalities, and participants pass many locations of local historical significance. description: The Pinåsløpet is a Norwegian uphill race that was started by Ole Wiik in 2002. The organizing clubs are Svarstad IL and Lardal o-lag. name: Byløpet
description: The city race features courses from 5 km to 21 km suitable for everyone, from professional runners to school classes and families. The race route takes place in scenic surroundings around Hjellevannet, with the venue located in the square outside Arkaden in Skien. name: Ørsta Fjellmaraton
description: Ørsta Mountain Marathon is a social and informal race in beautiful mountain scenery, with a low entry fee and a health obligation when you meet others on the trail. Whether you run fast, far, or just want to take a walk, we have a distance for everyone: a full marathon of 42 km for the toughest, a half marathon of 21 km which is our most popular distance, and a short course of 7 km for those who prefer shorter distances. There is also a children's race for those aged 3-12, where everyone receives a medal. The race is a tradition that has attracted an increasing number of participants since 2016, with magnificent mountain scenery and a great atmosphere.

Sognefjord Trail Run – Experience fjord and mountain from the trail!

Welcome!

The routes are varied and provide a great opportunity to experience the beautiful nature of the area.

With an elevation difference of 600 meters, the Birkebeinerløpet offers a varied and motivating training experience for both cross-country skiers, orienteers, and long-distance runners. In addition to the main race, the Halvbirkensom is also organized, which starts approximately halfway through the main course.

You can run four different distances: 1 km, 10 km, 20 km, or 30 km. The race is a true test of strength and a relatively challenging and technically demanding trail run, where runners alternate between running along the beaches and on forest paths. The goal of the race is to create as nice a route as possible around the entire Jeløy, passing over the three well-known peaks: Rødsåsen, Bjørnåsen, and Rambergtoppen.

The start and finish are at about 1000 meters above sea level, with the highest point at approximately 1743 meters above sea level. The course is about 14 km long.

Join us to celebrate the beauty of nature and the joy of movement – we promise an unforgettable experience!

name: FIL-mila
description: Get your running shoes ready and join us for the FIL-Mila in Lørenskog on Sunday, June 16th! The event is perfect for everyone, young and old, who loves running and exercise. Choose between the Filius children's race (approximately 400M), 3 km, and 10 km (with and without timing). The running routes are set in Losby and the entrance to the beautiful Østmarka National Park, and there will be a grill and refreshment station with the opportunity to buy something tasty to eat and drink. We promise a great atmosphere, plenty of running joy, and entertainment for the kids with our fantastic mascot, Filius!
course_highlights: The event is perfect for everyone, big and small, who loves running and exercise.
We will draw great prizes from our sponsors among all who register before May 15th!
There will be a grill and drink station with the option to purchase something good to eat and drink.

images.alt_text: Three children ready for the FIL-mile! Lørenskog, June 16th.

name: Randabergfjellet Opp
description: For the fourth year in a row, we are organizing the fun run Randabergfjellet Opp! This 3.4 km street race is suitable for absolutely everyone, from elite to amateur, from old to young. The race starts at the beautiful Tungenes Lighthouse and finishes at the top of Randabergfjellet, where we celebrate with a race party. After the award ceremony for Randabergfjellet Opp, we will also host the children's race Randabergfjellet Rundt, a highlight for many children.
course_highlights: This is a race that is suitable for absolutely everyone, from elite to amateur, from old to young.
The race starts at the beautiful Tungenes Lighthouse and finishes up at Randabergfjellet.
After the award ceremony for Randabergfjellet Opp, we will also host the children's race Randabergfjellet Rundt.

name: Beteberget Opp
description: "Beteberget Opp" was first held in August 2016. It is a mountain race that starts at Midtvangi in the valley bottom of Brydalen and ends on the mountain, 400 meters higher up. The course follows the road south along the valley bottom and up the mountain path to Bete, covering a distance of 3.8 km. This is a test of strength with an average incline of 15%, where the steepest section reaches a full 51%. The race is divided into competitive and recreational classes, making it suitable for both seasoned mountain runners and regular fitness enthusiasts.
course_highlights: The course goes through beautiful terrain and stunning primeval forest, ending with a magnificent view at the top.
In the competitive categories, there are cash prizes for podium placements in all classes and a prize for setting a new course record.
All participants, including those in the fitness classes, can win attractive raffle prizes.

images.alt_text: Runners in action during Beteberget Opp in Tynset.

name: Sommerkarusellen - 2. løp
description: Gneist Athletics welcomes you to the Summer Carousel 2024, a popular race series taking place during the summer months. There will be 5 races, 3 before the summer break and 2 after, with distances suitable for both beginners and experienced runners. Participants will have the opportunity to compete and improve their times in a social environment. Registration opened on April 1, and the first race kicks off on June 3.
course_highlights: The Summer Carousel offers a great opportunity to stay active and participate in a social environment.
Participants will have the opportunity to improve their times throughout the season.
Race numbers can be picked up at Fana Stadium on race day from 6:00 PM, with the first race starting at 5:00 PM.

images.alt_text: The start of a race with many participants. Great atmosphere!

name: Bislettmila
description: The Bislett Mile is a low-threshold athletics event where both elite athletes and recreational runners have the opportunity to run at Bislett Stadium. Elite heats are organized for senior men and women in the 5,000m and 10,000m, as well as 5 km and 10 km for recreational runners, with both genders competing in the same heat. This event provides an excellent opportunity to meet the national championship standard for the 10,000m, with good pacers present.
course_highlights: The Bislett Mile offers both elite athletes and recreational runners the opportunity to compete at Bislett Stadium.
Elite heats will be organized for senior men and women in the 5,000m and 10,000m events.
It will be an excellent opportunity to meet the national championship requirement for the 10,000m.

images.alt_text: To female runners during the Bislett Mile.

name: Odden Stafetten
description: Welcome to the Odden Relay 2025! This is a fun, informal, and social relay taking place on June 16, 2025, at Martodden/Norwegian Railway Museum in Hamar. The race features a varied and scenic course, where 4 people per team compete in both a long route (approximately 1.5 km) and a short route (just under 1 km). Participants will receive a bun and juice at the finish line, and there will be a prize draw after all teams have crossed the finish.
course_highlights: The stages run from the campsite towards the Railway Museum and the climbing park, with marked trails and marshals ensuring that you run the right way.
It’s a perfect opportunity to gather colleagues or friends for an active and fun afternoon.
Both corporate teams and friend teams are welcome, and the first leg is long, then short, then long again, and finally short.

name: Trønder-Østløpet
description: The Trønder-Østløpet, taking place on June 17, 2025, at 7:00 PM, has its origins in the athletics club of the same name and has been held in Hommelvik since 2016. The course has been redesigned to start and finish at Øya Stadium, which was completed in 2013, and the new route features a profile with little elevation change and long straight stretches that allow for maintaining high speeds. The race is a popular test for participants ahead of the St. Olavsloppet and offers distances of 5 km and 10 km.
course_highlights: The new course has been officially measured by avKondisLøypa and, as before, features a profile with minimal elevation change and long straight sections where it is possible to maintain high speed.
The race is used by many as a final test before they go out to measure their strength in the St. Olavsloppet, which starts in Trondheim shortly thereafter.
Sindre Johannessen was the best local runner in the 5 km, and Stian Oldervik was the best local runner in the 10 km.

name: Namdalskarusellen 5km
description: The Namdalskarusellen 5km is an exciting race that takes place in picturesque surroundings. Participants get to experience a varied course that combines both asphalt and gravel paths. The race is open to all ages and skill levels, making it a perfect opportunity for both beginners and experienced runners to take part.
course_highlights: Participation with timing and participation without timing.
The race is part of the Namdal Carousel, which includes several different distances and events.
The race takes place in Hestmarka, Namsos, and is part of a series that spans several months.

name: Holavatnet Rundt 10
description: The Summer Carousel Holavatnet Round was first organized in 1983 and is now in its 41st season. On average, about 130 people show up every Wednesday to exercise or test their fitness in the scenic course. The route goes around Holavatnet on asphalt and gravel paths, and it's easy to bring a stroller along for the round.
course_highlights: The course is 3.1 km long, consisting of 1.1 km of asphalt, 1.8 km of gravel road, and 0.2 km of asphalt.
There is a nature trail for children in the hiking class, with a prize located at the "cabin" (about 450 meters above sea level).
The race starts at about 40 meters above sea level, and the summit/finish is at 553 meters above sea level.

images.alt_text: Two runners in the Holavatnet round race.
