name: Skagerrakmila
description: On Friday, June 20, IK Grane Arendal Athletics invites you to a running festival in Arendal with the Skagerrakmila starting at 7 PM. For the 33rd time, the race is organized with the start and finish in the center of Arendal, taking you through the city center and nearby areas to the east. A June evening in Arendal often offers good weather, and together with the audience in the streets and on the outdoor terraces along the route, this creates a fantastic setting for the race. The Skagerrakmila is an annual 10 km race, and there will also be a 500-meter children's race held in conjunction with the event.
course_highlights: The Skagerrak Mile is an annual 10 km race in Arendal that was first held in 1990.
The race is certified as a quality event in the training magazine Kondis, and it holds a record for the number of participants from 1992 with 464 runners.
The fastest time is held by Urige Butas from Ethiopia, with 30:01 from 2005.

images.alt_text: Skagerrakmila winners on the podium in Arendal. Congratulations!

name: St. Hansgaloppen
description: The St. Hansgaloppen is a race that takes place in beautiful surroundings by Maridalsvannet. The course is relatively flat, with small elevation changes and a slight downhill at the turnaround point. Overall, it is an easy-to-run route that is suitable for both experienced runners and beginners. Øystein won the race with an impressive time of 50:00, thereby defending his title from the previous year.
course_highlights: The course is relatively flat, with small elevation changes and a slight downhill at the turnaround point.
Øystein defended his victory from last year and won the St. Hansgaloppen in a very good time.
The race includes a rerouted course that is approximately 175 meters longer than before.

name: Bèrghem Ultra Trail
description: Bèrghem Ultra Trail is an exciting ultramarathon that changes its route from year to year, but always takes place on the Hedmark plateau (Hedmarksvidda). This event, located in Brumunddal, celebrates and highlights the unique wilderness of Norway.
course_highlights: The Bèrghem Ultra Trail route changes from year to year.
The event always takes place on the Hedmark Plateau (Hedmarksvidda).
Our other ultra events celebrate and showcase the unique wilderness of Norway.

name: Norefjell Trail
description: Norefjell Trail is a true endurance test with a 42 km marathon that covers varied terrain, including mountain views, lakes, beautiful runnable trails, and gravel roads. The route passes Tempelseter and Istjenn, and reaches Høgevarde before descending to the finish line. This race is perfect for runners looking for a great challenge in Norway's beautiful mountain landscape.
course_highlights: 42 km | 1,550m elevation gain | ~80% trail | ~20% gravel.
The race starts and ends at Norefjell Ski & Spa, with a great warm-up during the first 3 km on gravel road up towards Leppejuvet.
The final stretch is more runnable, with open mountain trails towards Augunshaug along the ridge, before a technically challenging descent on rocky paths.

name: Fjord til Helvete
description: The mountain race From Fjord to Hell is organized by Søndre Land IL Athletics in collaboration with Søndre Land IL Ski. The race first took place in 2015 and will be held for the tenth time on Saturday, June 20, 2026. You can find more information about registration, class divisions, entry fees, and other event details on the race's Facebook page.
course_highlights: Organized by Søndre Land IL Athletics in collaboration with Søndre Land IL Ski.
The race saw the light of day in 2015.
Held for the tenth time on Saturday, June 20, 2026.

name: Chicken Bootcamp Race
description: Chicken Race is Norway's largest obstacle course for the whole family, held at a former military camp in Helgelandsmoen near Hønefoss, about 45 minutes from Oslo. Here, you can bring the whole family to courses filled with exciting challenges where you will run, climb, crawl, balance, carry heavy loads, and get both wet and dirty. The courses have just the right level of tough obstacles, and all of them are optional.
course_highlights: 2 km family run on Saturday, June 21, 2025, as well as 5 km and 8 km obstacle races.
Get wet, dirty, and infinitely tougher with us.
Norway's toughest running experience with mud, burpees, flames, bruises, and a sense of accomplishment.

name: Sommerskogsløpet
description: Welcome to the Sommerskogsløpet 2024. For the 29th time, the Sommerskogsløpet is being organized in beautiful natural terrain near Kristiansand city center. There are three different race distances that largely follow the Main Trail, and all routes converge at Dalane just north of the city center. This trail run offers a varied and scenic route that takes participants through forest paths and past stunning viewpoints, making it suitable for both experienced runners and beginners.
course_highlights: The Sommerskog Race takes place in beautiful natural terrain near the center of Kristiansand.
There are three different race distances that largely follow the Main Trail.
The race offers a varied and scenic route that takes participants through forest trails and past beautiful viewpoints.

name: Knarvik Maraton 5 km
description: Knarvik Marathon will be held on Saturday, June 21, 2025, featuring races for the marathon, half marathon, and 5 km. As part of the event, the Norwegian Championships in Half Marathon and NM 5 km road race will be organized. The start and finish for the 5 km is at Knarvik Stadium, and the course is relatively flat, with asphalt and gravel, winding around the stadium and through Brekkeløypa.
course_highlights: The 5 km course is easy to run and has its start and finish at Knarvik Stadium.
There is 1 aid station on the course, after approximately 3 km, and at the finish line, participants receive water and bananas.
The course is well marked with about 20 course marshals present, and the Red Cross will also be on site.

name: IDYLL Craft Run
description: IDYLL Festival and Craft Sportswear invite you to IDYLL x Craft Run 2024 at Dampskipsbrygga on June 22. Do you want to race against skiing stars? Now you have the opportunity! During IDYLL x Craft Run, you will have the chance to test your running skills against ski stars like Johannes Klæbo, Tiril Weng, and Even Northug, as well as other well-known figures from the national ski team. The race starts on Saturday, June 22, at 10:00 AM at Dampskipsbrygga.
course_highlights: Run towards the skiing stars like Johannes Klæbo, Tiril Weng, and Even Northug.
Test your running skills alongside well-known profiles from the national ski team.
The event takes place on Saturday, June 22, starting at 10:00 AM.

name: Flækøyhøe Upp
description: Flækøyhøe UPP is a mountain running event held in Skjåk, known as "spring's steepest adventure." The race starts at Bismo and goes through the center and along the walking and cycling path to Skamsarbrua, before taking you up to Morken farm and further into rugged terrain. Participants climb from 400 meters above sea level to the finish at a cairn at 1100 meters above sea level, at the border of Breheimen National Park. It is a great opportunity for both competition and socializing, with options for the whole family to participate.
course_highlights: The race offers challenging terrain and beautiful nature, attracting participants from near and far.
Participants in the recreational class can start between 8:00 AM and 10:00 AM without timing, while the competitive class starts at 11:00 AM.
New this year is that the fitness class can participate in a "Flækøyhøe Upp light" with the finish line at Øvre Flaten at approximately 620 meters above sea level.

name: Lundehøgda Opp
description: Welcome to Lundehøgda Opp on Saturday, July 1, 2023, at 11:00 AM, starting at Garveriet in Moelv town center. The course is marked from the finish line at Lundehøgda to the clubhouse in Amblisberget, where there are shower facilities and award distribution after the finish, around 1:30 PM. We will transport you to the top, and there will be a kiosk selling refreshments while you wait for the award ceremony. Course record holder and newly crowned Norwegian champion Geir Steig is registered!
course_highlights: There is a marked route from the finish line at Lundehøgda to the clubhouse in Amblisberget, where there are shower facilities and prize distribution as soon as possible after the finish.
Course record holder and recent Norwegian champion Geir Steig is registered!
Kiosk sales with refreshments while waiting for the awards ceremony in the clubhouse.

name: Bankmila
description: On Saturday, June 22, Surnadal IL and partner SpareBank 1 Nordmøre invite you to the fourth edition of Bankmila. The course, which starts at Skei and goes via Røtet and back to the finish line at Skei, is approximately 10 kilometers long. Bankmila is divided into Minibankmila for children, a recreational class, and a timed class, with start times from 11 AM. The organizers have a clear ambition to reach a three-digit number of participants this year, so mark Saturday, June 22, and join us for Bankmila!
course_highlights: The Minibank Mile starts at 11 AM, and participants are encouraged to arrive in good time for registration.
The recreational class starts at 11:30 AM, and the timed class starts at 12:00 PM.
The course is fast and easy to run, and it also promotes really good public health!

name: Knarvik Halvmaraton
description: Knarvik Half Marathon starts and finishes in the same place inside Knarvik Stadium. The course runs on roads in Knarvik and into the Brekkeløypa, where there is gravel, while the rest of the course is on asphalt. There are 8 aid stations along the route, and after crossing the finish line inside the stadium, water and bananas will be served. The course is well marked with approximately 20 course marshals present, and the Red Cross will also be on-site. The half marathon consists of 4 laps of the 5 km course, with an additional distance of 1097 meters onto the walkway towards Gjervik.
course_highlights: The course is car-free, and you can look forward to enjoying beautiful nature in your sight along the way.
There are 8 aid stations along the course, and after crossing the finish line inside the stadium, water and bananas will be served.
The age limit for participation is 15 years.

name: Bodø Bauta 6-timersløp
description: Bodø Bauta 24/12/6-hour race is an exciting event taking place in Bodø from June 22 to June 23, 2024. The race offers participants the opportunity to compete in three different distances: 24 hours, 12 hours, and 6 hours, providing both experienced runners and beginners the chance to participate. The event is held at Beddingen Cultural House, and it is a great opportunity for runners of all ages and skill levels to challenge themselves and experience the camaraderie of the race.
course_highlights: On Saturday, June 22, 2024, Bodø Bauta Running Club will host its very first 24-hour race.
With the midnight sun high in the sky, we hope for a magical atmosphere for both participants and the audience.
The event gives both experienced runners and beginners the chance to participate.

name: Midnight Sun Marathon
description: The Midnight Sun Marathon offers five distances and a unique experience under the midnight sun. In 2025, the race set a new participant record with nearly 9,000 runners from 88 nations. This is the world's northernmost marathon, certified by the Association of International Marathons and Distance Races (AIMS), and takes place annually in June in Tromsø. The race starts and finishes in Tromsø city center, featuring a scenic route that includes two crossings of the iconic Tromsø Bridge, providing participants with a rare opportunity to compete under the midnight sun.
course_highlights: The Midnight Sun Marathon offers a unique combination of nature, culture, and the joy of running, surrounded by mountains, fjords, and an Arctic summer where the sun shines all night.
The race features a large international starting field and is a highlight in the racing calendar for both experienced and new runners.
Participants get an amazing experience of running at night under a full moon, which creates a surreal atmosphere.

name: Nordmarka Skogsmaraton
description: We are looking forward to this year's most beautiful trail race, the Nordmarka Forest Marathon, which will be held for the 33rd time in 2026. It was a great day, and we hope that all runners had a wonderful racing experience. The course is challenging, and all honor and glory to everyone who lines up at the start! A big thank you to all our helpers, volunteers, and supporters – nothing happens by itself.
course_highlights: The race has tough courses, and we hope that all runners had a great racing experience.
We want to give honor and recognition to everyone who lines up at the start!
A big thank you to all our helpers, volunteers, and supporters – nothing happens by itself.

name: Sentrumsgateløpet
description: The City Center Run is a collaboration between Our City and the Kongsvinger Local Committee, offering a sporting street festival where everyone can participate. The race features officially measured distances of 5 km and 10 km, running on both sides of the Glomma River, with the 10 km race consisting of two laps on the same course. It is a beautiful route suitable for active individuals, recreational runners, city enthusiasts, and children, with a special children's race covering various distances (maximum 500 meters). The event also includes a market square, lively shops, and various children's activities.
course_highlights: The city center race features a beautiful course along the Glomma River and over both city bridges.
The race is for everyone: Both active runners, recreational joggers, city enthusiasts, and children.
Children's race with various distances (max 500 meters).

name: Sommernattsløpet Oslo
description: The Summer Night Run is the summer's most fun street race where you run on fast courses in beautiful surroundings. Swap your dress shoes for running shoes and join the summer's big running celebration at sunset! Whether you run 5 kilometers or 10 kilometers, we guarantee minimal elevation gain and maximum chance for a new personal best in the Summer Night Run. The course consists of a well-measured route of 5 kilometers and is Oslo's fastest course!
course_highlights: 5-kilometer course – full throttle in one lap!
The 10-kilometer course passes Filipstadkaia halfway and takes an extra loop in the route before the finish – twice the fun!

name: Kristinaløpet
description: The Kristina Run is a recreational race in the center of Tønsberg, organized by Tønsberg Athletics Club. In 2025, the race will take place on a new route starting and finishing at Kaldnes, an area well-suited for the event. The new course is flat and easy to run, encouraging fast times and records. The Kristina Run includes distances of 10 km, 5 km, and the Children's Kristina Run at 500 m.
course_highlights: The Kristinaløpet has been organized since 1981 and is named after Princess Kristina of Tunsberg.
The 10 km course consists of two laps of 5 km, with a separate recreational class for 5 km.
It is important to stay within the designated markers in the start and finish area, otherwise the time will not be recorded!

name: Veressjøen Rundt Mini
description: The Mountain Race Veressjøen Rundt, which was first held in 1974, has developed into a popular racing event with significant participation, even though the race was previously only open to runners from Verdal municipality. After a decline in interest in the 1980s, it was revitalized by enthusiasts from Helgådal IL who wanted to build up the "new Veresfestivalen" with a focus on the mountain village's nature and culture. The highlight came in 1995 when ski king Bjørn Dæhlie participated, and the race reached over 1086 participants. Veressjøen Rundt has been a community celebration that has maintained its popularity over the years, with a return to the traditional course around the lake for both recreational and competitive classes.
course_highlights: Veressjøen Rundt was among the 50 largest running events in the country in terms of participants during the 1990s.
The race was revitalized by passionate individuals from Helgådal IL who wanted to maintain the cultural and athletic quality of the event.
In 1995, skiing king Bjørn Dæhlie participated, and the race had a record attendance with 1,086 runners.

name: Isfjorden Skyrace
description: Isfjorden Skyrace 2024 is an exciting trail race with two distances: 16 km and 24 km. The race offers beautiful nature experiences and challenging courses, perfect for both beginners and experienced runners. Welcome to the 4th edition of Isfjorden Skyrace, taking place on June 21, 2025.
course_highlights: The race offers beautiful nature experiences.
Challenging courses for both beginners and experienced runners.
Two distances to choose from: 16 km and 24 km.

name: Skeikampen Dogrun
description: We are pleased to announce that the VOM Dogrun will be held at Skeikampen for the third time on June 8, 2025, starting at 7:00 PM. The VOM Dogrun is an event for all dogs, where participants can choose a class according to their own level, either with or without timing. A veterinarian will be present for animal welfare, and all participants will receive a VOM DOGRUN DOG LEASH, a bib number, and a medal. Prizes will be awarded to the fastest participants, and there will also be a raffle for prizes based on bib numbers for all classes.

There is always a veterinarian and a responsible person for animal welfare present at VOM DOGRUN.

The Oppdal Carousel is an annual race series organized by SenIL in collaboration with NOIL, now entering its 8th edition with five races spread throughout the season. Each stage has its own distance and unique route, attracting both local and visiting runners.

The popular race series starts with the first race of spring on April 19 and concludes with the final on September 6.

name: Perseløpet 5 km, 10 km, Halvmaraton
description: The Perseløpet 2025 is a fast and flat race, designed for records, with an AIMS-certified course. Participants can choose between 5 km, 10 km, half marathon, marathon, or 50 km, all within the same event. This is a low-threshold and inclusive race suitable for both recreational runners and those chasing a new personal best. There is a mass start for all distances, but with a mat start, you will receive your own start time when you cross the starting line. The course is known for a high percentage of personal records – maybe you'll set a new one?
course_highlights: Fast and flat course, designed for records.
Results available immediately after finishing.
Free parking.

name: Silsetvatnet Rundt
description: Silsetvatnet Rundt is a great hike around Silsetvatnet, where you can experience both cultural heritage sites, good fishing spots, and rest areas. The route mostly follows a solid gravel road but also includes trails. The paths are set in beautiful mountain terrain and are well-suited for a Sunday outing for the whole family, with distances of approximately 7.5 km for the hiking class and about 8.8 km for the active classes. The event takes place on Sunday, June 24, starting at Silsethytta from 11:00 AM.
course_highlights: The route mostly follows a solid gravel road, but includes sections of trail, and you will pass several cultural landmarks such as Silsethytta, Indergardssetra, and Gammelsetra.
The race courses are well-suited for a great Sunday outing for the whole family, with awards and a raffle for gift prizes based on the race numbers.
Freshly baked pastries and other kiosk items will be available for purchase at Silsethytta, which provides an extra cozy atmosphere for the event.

description: The Midsummer Run takes place on Thursday, June 23, and is the 42nd race in the series, a proud tradition in Hølonda. The course is just under 10 km and primarily runs through forest terrain, providing participants with a scenic experience. The recreational class has registration and starts from 5 PM to 6:30 PM, while the timed fitness class has registration open until the start at 7 PM. There will be prizes for the top three runners in the fitness class, as well as great raffle prizes in the recreational class.
course_highlights: The course is just under 10 km and primarily goes through forest terrain.
There are prizes for the top three runners in the recreational class: 1st place 800 NOK, 2nd place 500 NOK, 3rd place 300 NOK.
The recreational class has registration from 5 PM to 6:30 PM, and there are great raffle prizes.

description: Voss Running Carousel 4 is an exciting sports event taking place in Voss, Norway, welcoming participants and runners from the age of 9. The races occur on Mondays starting at 7 PM, with dates in 2026 including April 13, May 4, June 1, June 22, August 3, and September 21. The course is 5 km, with the start and finish at the sports field, and it goes through scenic areas such as Prestegardsmoen and along the waterfront promenade. There is a discount for those who register for all six races before the second race.

name: Bamford Frontyard
description: Bamford Frontyard consists of a relatively flat 3 km loop, where the first lap must be completed in 30 minutes. The next lap must be run 1 minute faster, and you must have completed all previous laps to continue. The competition ends when only one person finishes the final lap, and if multiple participants start, the fastest to finish will win. Completing 15 laps or more qualifies for the Ultra distance, and a medal is awarded to everyone who completes the first lap.
course_highlights: The first lap must be run in 30 minutes, and for each subsequent lap, the time is reduced by 1 minute.
The ranking is based on the number of completed laps within the time limit, and within each lap, the ranking is determined by the runner's time for that specific lap.
15 laps or more qualify for the Ultra distance.

The event will be held at Vestre Spone Sports Ground and also includes a children's race. Registration takes place at the start, and ice cream will be served after the finish.

description: The Kongsberg Motion Carousel is the final carousel event of the year, and the Lurdalsrunden was held in beautiful autumn weather. As usual, there were some challenges, possibly due to insufficient marking and eager youth, but all participants crossed the finish line. Kasper Lekve was the fastest in the short course with a time of 32:16, while Sofie Spiten and Kristian Qvenild were the fastest woman and man, respectively, with times of 1:00:16 and 55:40. The results can, as usual, be found on EQ Timing's pages.

The course is varied and challenging, with both flat sections and steep hills that provide participants with a good workout. The fun run/march is 4400 m long, starting and finishing at Furubakken sports ground, Valestrandsfossen.

name: Ottaløpet
description: Welcome to the Ottaløpet 2024, taking place on Saturday, June 29 in Otta, Gudbrandsdalen! The first edition was held in 1993, and the race includes 10 km and 5 km distances, as well as a non-timed fun run and a relay. The event focuses on involving the local community in an active day, with children's activities, music, and a pleasant atmosphere in the Park at the finish line. After a successful restart in 2022, we look forward to another exciting day with good weather and lively participation.
course_highlights: The Ottaløpet features both 10 km and 5 km distances, as well as a non-timed fitness class and a relay, and is open to both children and adults.

The award ceremony takes place in the Park, with prizes for 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place in both the 5 km and 10 km, as well as class winners in the 10 km.

name: Mensen Ernst Minneløp
description: The Mensen Ernst memorial run is a race for absolutely everyone, an event organized with a focus on health and well-being rather than on competition and performance. Here, we emphasize good vibes, joy of movement, and personal achievement! Regardless of age, fitness level, or experience, this race is perfect for YOU! Choose from several distances: 1.5km, 3.5km, 6.5km, 12km, relay, 400m children's race, 400m stroller race, and 400m wheelchair race.
course_highlights: The race honors the legendary achievement of Mons Øyri, who in 1832 ran from Paris to Moscow.
The Ernst Minneløp is a celebration of endurance and willpower, taking participants through beautiful and varied landscapes.
All the courses are named after Mensen Ernst's own running achievements and offer participants the opportunity to experience nature up close.

name: Arctic Backyard Kirkenes
location: Varmestuen til Kirkenes og omegn Skiklubb (KOS)
description: Arctic Backyard Kirkenes is a prominent event in the Kirkenes region's calendar, bringing together the local community and visitors for a day of athletic challenge and scenic enjoyment. This unique race offers various distances to accommodate all levels of experience, from a one-mile fun run to ultramarathon challenges, providing a perfect blend of competition and natural beauty. The race starts from the warming hut of the Kirkenes and Surroundings Ski Club (KOS) and takes participants along a picturesque route that winds around Andrevann. Participants must tackle laps of approximately 6.7 kilometers each, with the first lap starting at 12:00 PM, and they must complete each lap within an hour to progress to the next lap, with a maximum of 12 laps.
course_highlights: The race features a combination of asphalt and gravel roads, ensuring a dynamic running experience.
Participants must tackle laps of approximately 6.7 kilometers each, with the first lap starting at 12:00 PM.
The race offers a perfect blend of competition and scenic beauty, catering to all experience levels.

name: St Olavsloppet
description: St. Olavsloppet (formerly: St. Olofsloppet) is an annual road relay held at the end of June between Trondheim and Östersund, respectively in Trøndelag and Jämtland. In 2024, the 38th edition will take place from June 27 to June 29. The relay is named after King Olav Haraldsson, who was king of Norway from 1015 to 1028. The stages follow parts of the same route that the King took from Novgorod in Russia to Trøndelag in 1030 to Christianize Norway.
course_highlights: Thousands of runners are out on the roads between Trondheim and Östersund.
The relay is named after King Olav Haraldsson, who was king of Norway from 1015 to 1028.

This race, which is the 11th edition, has been held six times previously and offers a beautiful course through forest terrain. Participants can look forward to a dry and fast course with delightful late summer weather, and next year the course will be adjusted back to 50 km+.

name: Kristiansund Havmaraton
description: Kristiansund Sea Marathon is a trail race that was first organized by IL Norodd in Kristiansund in 2022, with the intention of becoming an annual event every July. The main race is 23 km, with additional distances of 13 km and 6 km, as well as a children's race of 500 m. The courses run along the coastline around the islands of Kirklandet, Gomalandet, and Skorpa, featuring varied terrain including asphalt, gravel, trails, and smooth rocks. The start and finish for all distances are at Atlanten Stadium, and the next race will take place on June 28, 2025.
course_highlights: The main race is 23 km, with additional distances of 13 km and 6 km, as well as a children's race.
The coastal marathon route mainly runs along the shoreline around the islands of Kirklandet, Gomalandet, and Skorpa.

name: Svartløken Rundt
description: Svartløken Rundt is a trail run that was first held in 2003 and has now been part of Tomrefjord IL's anniversary celebration. The event is open to the whole family and includes a hike, children's race, cycling, fitness class, and competitions. The main race is 13.4 km long, while there is also a shorter loop of 4.5 km and a children's race of about 500 meters. The course network is of high standard, featuring both classic track and freestyle routes.
course_highlights: The children's race of about 500 meters takes place in the area around the warming hut, and there is also a sledding hill for the kids.
Seniors and youth run the "main race" around Svartløken, which is 13.4 km long, while age-specific classes and the fitness class compete on the lighted trail (4.5 km).

name: Oslo Bergen Trail
description: Oslo Bergen Trail is a trail ultramarathon from Oslo to Bergen, taking place from July 2-10, 2021. The course is approximately 515 km long with a total elevation gain/loss of 18,000 meters, following marked hiking trails (DNT trails) where possible. In some short sections, the route goes off-trail or follows only a faint path. This is a team competition where each team can consist of 2 or 3 members.
course_highlights: The route for the Oslo Bergen Trail is approximately 515 km long and has a total elevation gain/loss of 18,000 meters.

The marathon distance will start back at Laukvika, and a bus to the start is included for all participants. The route goes over Matmora, up from Haugen Gård, past Botnvatnet, and ends in Svolvær after covering approximately 2000 meters of elevation gain. The age limit for participation is 18 years.

Here, both adults and children can participate in various distances, including marathon, half marathon, 10 km, 5 km, and a "Miniton" of 4.2 km. The courses run along Jølstravatnet, and there are opportunities for both competition and fitness. Awards are presented at the finish line, and result lists will be available at Jølstrahallen.
course_highlights: Jølster Marathon is one of Norway's most traditional races!
The trails run through beautiful West Coast nature.

name: Bitihorn Opp
description: Welcome to an informal and casual uphill race up Bithihorn. Whether you walk or run, fast or slow, everyone is welcome. The course runs on stone steps and trails on the front side of Bithorn, with a distance of 2 kilometers and an elevation gain of 450 meters. The race takes place on Saturday, July 5, 2025, starting at 12:00 PM, and there will be prizes, good vibes, and spectacular views at the top.
course_highlights: The course is approximately 2 km with 450 meters of elevation gain and is suitable for both hikers and competitive runners.
The hike to the top of Bitihorn offers magnificent views of Jotunheimen and large parts of Valdres.
It is a moderately challenging summit hike with a clear trail and no special difficulties.

name: Ålgård-Sirdal 100K
description: Ålgård-Sirdal 100K is a challenging course of 100 kilometers that takes participants from Ålgård to Sirdal. The route is varied, featuring both mountains and roads, and the last aid station is at Lortabu (86 km). After this, the course follows the road to Gravassryggen, before ascending the steep trail to Storeknut. Towards the end of the race, participants will experience a fantastic view over Sirdal from the finish line at Slottet.
course_highlights: The last aid station is at Lortabu (86 km), where the route then follows the road to Gravassryggen.
After 90 km, the participants will understand why the trail gets its name from the 1800s, when shepherds had to herd their sheep from the coast to the mountain pastures in Sirdal.
About 1 km before the finish, there is a steep gravel path leading to the finish at the Castle, where you get a fantastic view of the entire Sirdal.

description: Rødtangen Rundt 2024 was a success! With 144 participants in the main race and 55 participants in the children's races, we have reached levels from before the pandemic. The event took place in beautiful Holmsbu, and both young and old experienced the joy of participating in the race.

name: Preikestolen Trailrun
description: The Preikestolen Trailrun is an epic running journey where you follow in the footsteps of Rockman, the legendary figure who braved the rugged trails every weekend in pursuit of winning his beloved's heart, but without swimming. This race is not just a run – it is a mythical adventure where you battle against the forces of nature on some of the world's most spectacular trails. Prepare for a mix of skyrunning, technical trail running, and exhilarating climbing, as you run through mystical forests, cross boulder fields, and ascend to the mountain peaks above the Lysefjord. The route takes you on a secret path to the iconic Preikestolen, before descending into a playground of ancient, rugged terrain.
course_highlights: You will run through mystical forests, cross moors, and ascend to the mountain peaks above the Lysefjord, where the shimmering water is framed by majestic cliffs.
The route takes you along a secret outer trail to the iconic Preikestolen, before descending into a playground of ancient, rugged terrain – shaped by the gods themselves.
This race is extremely technical with an elevation gain of 1200 meters and a distance of 20 km.

name: Hornindal Rundt
description: Hornindal Rundt is an annual ultra mountain race held in Hornindal, situated between Jotunheimen and the North Sea. The race, which was first organized in 2010, offers two distances: a 75 km ultra mountain race with 5600 meters of elevation gain and a 38 km mountain race with 2900 meters of elevation gain. Participants in the 75 km will navigate through 20 mountain checkpoints and experience a nature that can only be found in fairy tales. Starting from Honndalshallen at 07:00, this is a challenge that gives goosebumps to all who take part.
course_highlights: Hornindal Rundt is known as Norway's toughest mountain race, with 75 km and 5600 meters of elevation gain.
The race goes through 20 mountain checkpoints, providing participants with a unique experience of the spectacular nature in the area.
In 2016, Hornindal Rundt was part of the Norwegian Championships in ultrarunning.

name: Jomfrulandsløpet
description: The Jomfruland Race is open to everyone, including those who are not affiliated with a sports club. The "classic" race is 10 km long, consisting of two laps on a 5-kilometer course. It is also possible to participate in one lap, which is 5 km with timing. The course is on flat ground, gravel, and forest trails, and it all takes place on the beautiful island of Jomfruland off the coast of Kragerø.
course_highlights: The race is open to everyone, including those who are not affiliated with a sports club.
The "classic" Jomfrulandsløpet is 10 km long and consists of two laps in a 5-kilometer course.

name: Feriespretten
description: Feriespretten is a traditional trail race that has been organized by Hope IL for 34 years. The race features two distances: a long course of approximately 9 km and a short course of about 5 km, both set in varied, hilly terrain. It is scheduled for Tuesday, July 9, 2024, at 5:59 PM (GMT+2) in Sandnes, Norway, with a mass start and 135 participants. Feriespretten is known for its festive atmosphere, even in challenging weather conditions such as rain.
course_highlights: The race has attracted both young and experienced runners, and there has been a record number of participants this year.
Trim trail: If you don't want to be timed, you can still participate as a recreational runner in the short course.
The race is timed using RFID technology and utilizes Webscorer PRO 6.9 for the results.

description: The inspiring charity race Dream Challenge takes place in Lillesand on Saturday, July 13. Dream Challenge is not just a race, but also a fundraising campaign where all proceeds go directly to Star for Life's work with youth in South Africa – training with purpose. We encourage everyone to participate on this day, where we combine physical activity with support for a good cause. This is an event for the whole family! Bring friends and family and join as runners, support crew, or cheer squad.
course_highlights: All funds go directly to Star for Life's work with youth in South Africa – training with purpose.

name: Oslo Bergen Trail
description: Oslo Bergen Trail is a trail ultramarathon from Oslo to Bergen, taking place from July 2-10, 2021. The course is approximately 515 km long with a total elevation gain/loss of 18,000 meters, and follows marked hiking trails (DNT trails) where possible and appropriate. In some short sections, the route goes through forest and mountain terrain without a trail or follows only a faint track. The organizer may activate alternate routes under difficult weather conditions.

The course is approximately 515 km long with a total elevation gain/loss of 18,000 meters.

This event attracts athletes and outdoor enthusiasts from near and far, eager to test their limits and experience the raw beauty of the Norwegian wilderness. The courses run through easy terrain, mostly on gravel roads and trails in beautiful natural areas near Nevlunghavn, Mølen, and Helgeroa. name: Kvasshovden Opp
description: Kvasshovden Opp is a mountain running race organized by Ulvik Idrettslag, which was first held in 2008. The race has since become a great success, with over 500 participants in 2009 and has been part of the Powerade Norwegian Cup in mountain running. The course starts in the center of Ulvik at about 10 meters above sea level and finishes at the top of Kvasshovden, 1030 meters above sea level, over a distance of 7.5 km. At the top, a fantastic view of the western Norwegian fjord landscape awaits.
course_highlights: The course has a length of 7.5 km and ascends from 0 to 1030 m.a.s.l.
The race is known for its steep and rocky terrain, and the record from the center to the top is under an hour.
Participants can enjoy a spectacular view of the fjord landscape from the top, as well as pass several beautiful mountain pasture areas and local farms along the way.

description: Sunnfjord Ultra is an ultramarathon taking place on July 12, 2025, starting in Førde and finishing in Rivedal. The course is 53 km long and classified as trail running with a total elevation gain of 2000 meters. It consists of 13 km of gravel road, 20 km of asphalt, and 20 km of trail, where the first 11 km is a mix of gravel and farm road. Participants have 13 hours to complete the race and will receive a finisher t-shirt, a medal, as well as a special gift for the winners in both the men’s and women’s categories.

name: Espe Rundt
description: Espe Rundt is a 7 km fitness run held every week from Easter to moose hunting season, with a mass start at 6:00 PM every Thursday from Nordåsveien 43 in Birkeland. The course goes up Nordåsstien, continues towards Haugevann, and around Espe before returning to the start. Participation is free of charge, but a small fee is required for prizes in the final race. All results are published on the Espe Rundt Facebook page and in Birkenesavisa.
course_highlights: The course is exactly 7050 m, and the record is held by Hans Gunnar Omdal from Vindbjart with a time of 28:51 set on July 1, 2004.
There is room for everyone who wants a nice trip on a very special course, and the race is best suited for the fit hiker or runner.
You must have completed 3 races to be counted in the final, which is a reverse chase start based on the average of your three best races throughout the summer.

name: Kvitfjell Opp
description: Kvitfjell Opp is one of the summer's most brutal uphill races, where we turn the Olympic course upside down and run from the finish at the bottom to the start at the top. The course is 3.2 kilometers long with an elevation gain of 838 meters, following the downhill track used during the 1994 Olympics. Participants will encounter challenging sections such as Mæhlumshenget, Tommy Moe, and Wintherhugget, and the feeling of reaching the top is indescribable!
course_highlights: The course follows the downhill track that was used during the 1994 Olympics and is currently used in connection with the World Cup.

The course mainly follows marked trails in the mountain area around Kvitfjell, and the race takes place both above and below the tree line, with the highest point at about 1100 meters above sea level. Even though it is mid-summer, it can be wise to be prepared for weather changes.
course_highlights: Kvitfjell Running Festival has been delivering legendary running experiences since 2021, featuring Northern Europe's steepest ski slope and prime trails in the heart of Norwegian nature.
The course is approximately 25 kilometers long, with 19 kilometers on trails and 6.5 kilometers on road.
In 2024, the festival will expand with yet another race, namely the Stuttlaupet.

name: Jordbærdilten
description: The Strawberry Run and the Mini Run are two separate races taking place in Valldal. The Mini Run starts at 2:45 PM, while the Strawberry Run starts at 3:30 PM. Both races have their start and finish at Rådhusmarka, and there will be an awards ceremony at the pier after the race.
course_highlights: The mini race starts at 2:45 PM.
The Strawberry Run starts at 3:30 PM.
Start and finish at Rådhusmarka, with award ceremony at the quay.

name: Rondane Backyard Trail
description: Rondane Backyard Trail is a "last human standing" backyard race organized by Hell Ultraløperklubb, taking place from July 26 to 27, 2025, in the Kroktjønna area around Folldal IF's ski arena in Stormoegga. The race starts on Saturday at 10:00 AM, and in the first year, a 24-hour backyard format will be held. The winner will be the one who completes the most laps in the shortest time, and everyone who finishes at least one lap will receive a medal. The 6.7 km course runs on forest trails, gravel paths, and asphalt, and there will be good facilities available during the race.
course_highlights: The race features a 6.7 km loop that must be completed as many times as possible within 24 hours.
Prizes are awarded for the overall winners and sprint bonuses for the best female and male competitors.
The Stormoegga ski arena has a great service building with a lounge area, kitchen, restrooms, changing rooms, and shower facilities.

name: Sørlandstesten 11
description: The Sørlandstest is a low-threshold recreational race for everyone who wants a positive running experience, regardless of ambition level. Whether you are training for a bigger goal, feeling the competitive nerves, or just want a social and active day – this is the race for you! There is room for both beginners and experienced runners, and the most important thing is that you show up with a good mood and a desire to run. We cheer just as much for the one who crosses the finish line first as for the one who completes their very first race.
course_highlights: The Sørlandstest offers a flat and fast course up Setesdalsveien to Strai, before participants turn around and run back.
The race features distances of 5 km, 10 km, and a 600 m children's race, making it accessible for all ages and skill levels.
The start and finish are located on the opposite side of the road from Gumpens Auto, providing a simple and accessible location in Kristiansand.

name: Løp til Verdens Ende
description: Run to the World's End is a duathlon where teams of two run trail and swim in open water, without a break between the two disciplines. The running distance is longer than a full marathon, in addition to eight kilometers in the water. According to the organizer, this is a fantastic way to utilize the archipelago, but there is no room for transitions between the two activities, so participants must run and swim in wetsuits and running shoes. It is recommended to use flotation devices to make it easier.
course_highlights: Duathlon with trail running and open water swimming without breaks between the disciplines.
The race distance is longer than a full marathon, in addition to eight kilometers of swimming.
Participants must wear a wetsuit and running shoes, and it is recommended to use flotation devices.

name: Meråker Mountain Challenge NM
description: Meråker Mountain Challenge is a trail ultra-run that features a 70-kilometer route with nearly 4000 meters of elevation gain. The race traverses varying terrain such as marshland, slippery rock faces, and steep hills, and participants must be prepared for challenging conditions like fog and slippery sections. Unique aspects of the race include transportation to the starting area by RIB boat, which adds an extra dimension to the experience. We look forward to welcoming even more runners to Meråker and Teveltunet in 2026, and registration is now open.
course_highlights: The race features a 70-kilometer route with nearly 4000 meters of elevation gain.
Participants must be prepared for challenging conditions, including fog and slippery sections.
Unique features of the race include transportation to the starting area by RIB boat.

name: Kongsvinger Skogsmaraton
description: Kongsvinger Forest Marathon is Inland's only and Norway's second forest marathon, taking place on August 3, 2024. Here you can choose from many different distances, including the full marathon, half marathon, and Kongsvingermila. Experience an unforgettable day filled with joy, community, and competition in a hilly and varied forest area north and west of Sæter farm. The marathon course follows forest roads and good trails, and there are 3 aid stations along the route.
course_highlights: Kongsvinger Forest Marathon offers distances of 42.2 km, 21.1 km, 10 km, and 4.2 km.
The marathon route runs through a hilly, varied, and beautiful forest area, with the main course following forest roads and good trails.
There are 3 water stations set up for participants during the race.

name: Gaea Norvegica Trail
description: Gaea Norvegica Trail is a multi-day, self-supported race, known as Norway's longest and toughest ultra. There are two routes: the first is 400 kilometers long and the second is 600 kilometers long, both completed over a 5-day period. The race is ITRA-certified and offers 6 UTMB points. Are you brave enough to take on nature and see how you fare? Join us and experience the stunning beauty of Norwegian nature while following the geological Oslo Rift formation from Oslo to Hamar.
course_highlights: The route follows the Akerselva river to Maridalsvannet, continues into Nordmarka up to Eidsvoll, and then heads northeast before ending at Hedmarksvidda.
The total elevation gain in the race is 8300 meters, and assistance is not allowed; participants must carry all clothing, food, and drink in their backpacks.
Gaea Norvegica Trail is ITRA-certified and offers 6 UTMB points, making it a challenging experience for ultrarunners.

name: Altamila 10km Gateløp
description: Altamila is a running event that takes place every year on the first weekend of August. The event consists of three main distances, as well as a children's race: Sport 1 Alta Half Marathon - 21.1 km, Advanti Altamila - 10 km, and Fun Run - 5 km (without timing). Both Advanti Altamila and Sport 1 Alta Half Marathon are certified by a certified course measurer from the Norwegian Athletics Association and have been described as very fast and easy to run courses, with great opportunities to set personal records.
course_highlights: Advanti Altamila and Sport 1 Alta Half Marathon have been officially measured by a certified course measurer from the Norwegian Athletics Association.
The courses are described as very fast and extremely runnable.
Here are great opportunities to set personal records.

name: Møkster Maraton
description: Welcome to Møkster Marathon! The race takes place on Saturday, August 9, 2025, and this is the 13th time the event is being held. Møkster is a beautiful, small island at the edge of the sea, located in Austevoll municipality south of Bergen. Here, participants can experience stunning nature, a guest harbor, a shop, and a restaurant. The routes traverse fields and roads, asphalt and gravel, through farmyards and along old farm roads, providing an absolutely extraordinary experience.
course_highlights: Møkster Marathon was held for the first time on Saturday, August 4, 2012, and it became an unforgettable day for organizers, spectators, and runners.
The race goes over fields and roads, asphalt and gravel, through farmyards and along old farm roads.
Møkster is a small island with about 35 permanent residents and a large group of cabin owners, all with a high percentage of passionate individuals.

name: Skeikampen Rundt
description: Skeikampen Rundt is a trail run set in scenic surroundings of small forests and bare mountains around Skeikampen. The course is approximately 12.2 km long and ascends to 347 meters, and it can be run in either direction, with a descent regardless of the route chosen. The run is moderately challenging and suitable for children, but everyone must enjoy downhill runs. It offers fantastic views of the mountain landscape, including Jotunheimen and Rondane, and concludes with waffles and coffee at one of the cozy mountain cafés.
course_highlights: The trail ascends to the trail junction at Torsdalsleitet, where you get a fantastic view of the surrounding mountains.
The trip is moderately challenging and suitable for children, but everyone must enjoy downhill runs.

name: Backyard Trondheim Ultra
description: Ready for a new round of the Muruvik Backyard Ultra? The race was first held in the spring of 2021, and now it’s finally time to host the first race in Trondheim. The course is an out-and-back route from Muruvik to Hommelvik along the picturesque Malvikstien, a flat course with great record potential. Runners have one hour to complete a 6.7 km loop, and every full hour, the race starts anew. The winner is the one who ultimately lasts a round alone, and a maximum of twelve rounds is set, which gives a total distance of 80.4 km.
course_highlights: The course runs back and forth between Muruvik and Hommelvik along the idyllic Malvik Trail, a flat route with great record opportunities.
The laps start every hour on the hour, and your pace determines how long of a break you get before the next start.
All runners are welcome, and whether you participate to run a lap or to steel yourself for victory, it is set up as a social event with a low entry threshold.

name: Trysil Trail
description: Experience trail running, community, and mountain adventures in Trysil! Trysil Trail by HOKA is organized in collaboration with Marathongruppen, ensuring a professional and seamless experience from start to finish. Trysil Trail is more than just a race – it’s a weekend filled with after-run activities, social runs, training sessions, and an equipment fair. Whether you are a beginner or an experienced runner, inspiring experiences and nature encounters await you in the spectacular mountain landscape.
course_highlights: Trysil Trail is not just race day – it’s a weekend of running, community, and incredible experiences.
The weekend offers camaraderie, after run, and memorable experiences, in addition to two races through beautiful terrain.
Trysil Trail 14K starts in Fageråsen and follows the Mountain Loop, while the 24K has an additional detour around Skrufjellet.

name: Bodøryggen
description: Bodø Run Bodøryggen, which takes place on Saturday, October 1st, is a majestic mountain race of approximately 21 kilometers from Skaug to Bestemorenga in Bodømarka. This race offers a beautiful trail with fantastic views of the Vestfjord, Lofoten Wall, and the city of Bodø. Bodøryggen is a challenging yet rewarding journey with about 1,000 meters of elevation gain, perfect for experienced hikers looking for a memorable experience.
course_highlights: Start at Skaug, steeply up to Skaugtuva before it levels out and the journey can be enjoyed along Bodøryggen / Løpsfjellet.
Bodøryggen offers a spectacular view of the Vestfjord, the Lofoten Wall, the city of Bodø, and Børvasstindan.
The trail is well marked, but sturdy hiking shoes and necessary equipment are recommended due to the length and elevation changes.

name: Henningsvær Halvmaraton
description: Welcome to the Henningsvær Half Marathon – one of the most scenic races in Norway! The course starts in the small fishing village of Henningsvær and takes you past dramatic coastlines with towering peaks behind you. Whether you are chasing results or just want to enjoy the view, this race is for you. The route begins at the Trevarefabrikken, continues to the end of Henningsvær, before you run back out of the village and along the coastal road towards Rørvika Strand by the E10. When you return to Henningsvær, you will take a lap inside the village before heading towards the finish at the Trevarefabrikken.
course_highlights: The course takes you past dramatic coastlines and high peaks.
Automatic timing with split times at turnaround point.
Henningsvær is a vibrant community with many visitors.

name: Sommerkarusellen - 4. løp
description: The 4th race in this year's Head Energy Summer Carousel was held in Bergen and started in beautiful sunshine with around 20 degrees, but ended with heavy rain. Anders Staude from Gular won the race with a time of 16:40, while Rebecca Hilland from Bergen Running Club took the victory in the women's category with 17:57. A total of 222 runners completed the second to last race in the series, with 99 runners finishing the 5 km and 33 completing the double distance of 10 km.
course_highlights: Anders Staude from Gular was the fastest of all when he won the 4th race in this year's Summer Carousel with a time of 16:40.
Rebecca Hilland from Bergen Running Club won the women's category with a time of 17:57.

The races take place on Mondays starting at 7 PM, with dates in 2026 including April 13, May 4, June 1, June 22, August 3, and September 21. The course is 5 km, starting and finishing at the sports field, then one lap in Prestegardsmoen, continuing along the waterfront promenade and back to the sports field.
course_highlights: The route goes through scenic areas such as Prestegardsmoen and along the waterfront promenade.
The event is open to participants from 9 years and older.
There is a discount for those who register for all six races before the second race.

name: Solan Gundersens Bergmaraton
description: Solan Gundersens Mountain Marathon takes place in Alvdal on August 16, 2025, with the start and finish at Steimoegga Sports Facility. Participants can choose between distances of 1 km, 6 km, half marathon (22 km), and full marathon (48 km). The race is open to children, youth, and adults, and offers a challenging experience through Alvdal's beautiful hills and mountains, including Sten, Brannvålsberget, Baugsberget, Storfjellet, Kvebergsberget, and Høståsen. There will be food and drink stations along the route, but it is recommended to bring your own drink between the stations.
course_highlights: The 48 km competition and the 22 km fun run start at 09:30.

description: Navy Race is an obstacle course that combines exciting land and water-based challenges with an atmosphere filled with community and joy. Whether you are an experienced athlete, a casual exerciser, or a beginner, there is a place for you here – alone or as part of a team. The 8 km course takes you through the old naval base with 30 obstacles, where you will tackle everything from climbing walls and crawling in sand to wading in water. Join for a weekend filled with adrenaline, laughter, and camaraderie, and experience something truly unique as you cross the finish line.
course_highlights: Navy Race presents you with challenges that test both physical and mental strength.
The course takes you through iconic areas as you tackle spectacular military obstacles.
Experience a weekend filled with adrenaline, laughter, and camaraderie.

The event has received praise for its friendly volunteers and impeccable service, although the asphalt sections can be challenging for the knees. With well-known peaks like Ryksåsen, Hvittingen, Montebello, Skibergfjell, and Snippane, this is a race for those seeking a hardcore ultra trail experience.
course_highlights: The 75 km ultramarathon included 7 of the 10 peaks and took participants through a variety of beautiful locations around Hof.
The officials were friendly and the service was impeccable; overall, it was a very good event.

name: Hardanger Halvmaraton
description: Øystese Sports Club invites athletes to a peaceful race along the fjord with a view of the glacier. It is a fast course exclusively on asphalt, passing by orchards, densely built areas, and a bustling town center along the route. The start and finish are at the beautiful Storeteigen village museum, and the course has a total elevation gain of 141 m over 21.1 km. You will pass well-maintained cultural landscapes, and safe crossings will be ensured with well-marked road intersections.
course_highlights: The route passes by orchards and densely populated areas, and offers a view of the glacier.
The start and finish line is at the beautiful Storeteigen Rural Museum.
The course has a total elevation gain of 141 m over 21.1 km and runs on asphalt, primarily on a wide pedestrian and bicycle path.

This is the race for you if you want a fast yet challenging run in the terrain.

name: Grue Backyard
description: The ultramarathon Grue Backyard is completed over 12 laps of 6.7 km each, with a new start every hour. The first lap starts at 09:00, with 1 hour between each lap, and the twelfth and final lap starts at 20:00. If no one finishes the last lap, there are no winners. If multiple participants complete all laps, the winner is the one who crosses the finish line first in the last lap.

name: Backyard Tromsø Ultra
description: Tromsø Backyard Ultra is a very special ultramarathon where participants run a loop every hour. When a new lap begins, you must be ready at the starting line again. The course, which is 6.7 km long, takes you through varied and challenging terrain with a mix of gravel roads and trails, offering stunning views of Kvaløya and Hamna. With 188 meters of elevation gain per lap, the route features both technical sections and flow segments, creating a spectacular setting for a true northern Norwegian backyard ultra race.
course_highlights: The course takes you through a varied and challenging terrain with a mix of gravel road and trail.
The route goes uphill through Granåsen and Myrbakken, and further north along trails with a stunning view of Kvaløya and Hamna.
With 188 meters of elevation gain per lap, the course offers both technical sections and flow segments.

name: Mjøsen Backyard Race
description: With 12 laps and a total of 2856 meters of elevation gain, Mjøsen Backyard takes you through a challenge equivalent to running from the deepest point of Lake Mjøsa up to the water surface six times. This is the race for you who want to challenge both body and willpower, and experience the joy of mastering one of Norway's most unique racing concepts. How long can you keep moving? The laps start every hour on the hour, and your pace determines how long your break is before the next start.
course_highlights: Mjøsen Backyard is a backyard race consisting of laps of 6.7 km that are run up to twelve times.
The race starts and ends at a gathering place with a refreshment station, restrooms, and a chair to sit on.
Even though the ultimate goal is to reach 80.4 km, you are warmly welcome to run as many laps as you want – or can manage.

name: Lavterskel-løpet Sirkus
description: The low-threshold race Sirkus will be held on August 10, 2025, in Sørmarka, Stavanger. The course is 6.36 kilometers long with an elevation gain of 176 meters, taking you from the start at the parking lot to Ullandhaugtårnet up to the finish line at the top of Ullandhaugtårnet, featuring a mix of gravel and asphalt. There are many ups and downs, but the course runs through Stavanger's most beautiful surroundings. Additionally, there will be a children's race of 700 meters for kids aged 2 to 9, starting at 11:00 AM.
course_highlights: The course is 6.36 kilometers long and has an elevation difference of 176 meters.
The course runs through Stavanger's most beautiful surroundings.
There will be a children's race of 700 meters for kids aged 2 to 9 years.

name: Follaheiløpet
description: The Follaheiløpet was first held in August 2009, starting from Follafoss. The race is scheduled to take place on Sunday, August 9, 2020, and in 2019, 34 participants competed in the competitive classes and 80 in the recreational class under splendid weather and conditions. Ole Jørgen Bruvoll and Marte Elden were the clear winners of the uphill race.
course_highlights: The Follaheil Race was first held in August 2009.
The race starts from Follafoss.
In 2019, there were 34 participants registered in the competitive classes and 80 in the recreational class.

name: Fevik Løbestævne
description: Fevik Running Festival is an annual race event held at Fevik Stadium. The event includes distances of 3,000, 5,000, and 10,000 meters, and it is open to everyone, regardless of level. Participants have the opportunity to compete in beautiful surroundings, making it a popular event among both beginners and experienced runners.
course_highlights: Everyone is welcome to run 3,000, 5,000, and 10,000 meters on Sunday, October 12 at Fevik Stadium.
Just show up in good time before 12:00, when the 3,000m and 5,000m runners start, and at 12:45 the 10,000m begins.
Registration takes place before the start and is free, and participants are encouraged to bring friends to cheer or join in.

name: Tromsø Løpefest
description: Tromsø Running and Roller Ski Festival 2025 🏃‍♀️🏃‍♂️ is a sports collaboration between the clubs in Tromsø and takes place on Sunday, August 10. Welcome to a fast 5-kilometer race and roller ski race (the roller ski race is 5 km / 3 km depending on age). The event supports the joy of running, the skiing community, public health, and the local sports environment, and occurs simultaneously with the Arctic Race's final stage in Tromsø. The race is for participants aged 12 and older, and everyone who finishes will receive a medal.
course_highlights: The race and roller ski race are organized by BUL Tromsø, MSM, Tromsø Running Club, Northern Runners, TUIL Running, Tromsø Ski Club, and Tromsø Biathlon Club.
The course is officially measured, and there will be awards in the women's and men's categories.
All participants will be offered drinks and fruit in the finish area.

name: Grønliåsen Rundt
description: Grønliåsen Rundt is a hilly and quite challenging trail race that carries prestige for having completed it. The courses take participants through scenic surroundings with varied landscapes, including both challenging hills and flat sections, providing a good mix of physical challenge and nature experience. Challenge your neighbor, colleague, or buddy to join in!
course_highlights: Grønliåsen Rundt is a hilly and quite challenging course that carries prestige for having completed it.
The courses take participants through varied landscapes with both challenging hills and flat sections.
The local trail run Grønliåsen around has been organized several times, and many recreational runners appreciate a locally sourced race in the beautiful local areas.

name: Tittinghalla Rundt
description: Tittinghalla Rundt is a traditional fitness race in Inderøy, first held in 1966. The course is 13.5 kilometers long, mostly on roads, but with some forest trail descending from the highest point of the course, Ørdalen - Inderøy's answer to the Geiranger view. Participants in the recreational class can start whenever they want between 10 AM and 12 PM from Utøy school.
course_highlights: The course is 13.5 kilometers long.
It is mostly along the road, but with some forest trail down from the highest point of the course.
In the fitness class, one can start whenever they want between 10 AM and 12 PM from Utøy school.

name: Oslo Østmarka Halvmaraton
description: Østmarka Half Marathon takes place from July 31 to August 9, with a mass start on August 9 at 11:00 AM. The start and finish are at Rustadsaga, and the race covers varied terrain including gravel, trail, and asphalt. There will be awards based on strong performances, random draw competitions, and contests on the websites during the race festival.
course_highlights: The mass start takes place on August 9th at 11:00 AM.
The race takes place on varied surfaces such as gravel, terrain, and asphalt.
There will be prizes awarded based on good performances and random draw competitions.

name: Disirunden
description: The Disirunden and Disimila 2025 will take place on Saturday, August 10, 2025, at 11:00 AM, starting from Disenå Community Center, Finnholtvegen 91, Disenå, Kongsvinger, Norway. This race has previously seen impressive performances, such as when Elise Mobrenna (13) set a course record in her first participation. With 83 registered participants and the official opening of the activity and training arena, Disenå IL promises to promote physical activity in the local community.
course_highlights: Elise Mobrenna (13) set a course record in her first participation in the Disirunden.
There are 83 registered participants for the race.
Disenå IL promises to foster physical activity with the official opening of the activity and training arena.

name: Harstadkarusellen Rundt
description: Harstadkarusellen / autumn series offers weekly physical and virtual races leading up to Christmas, with both short and long courses. The physical races take place on Mondays, while the virtual ones can be completed from Monday to Sunday. The races are open to everyone, regardless of age and fitness level, and participants can either record their own time or take part without timing. There is also an opportunity for organized course previews before the race, and prizes for participation in multiple races are available.
course_highlights: Participants can record their own time, and it is possible to participate without recording a time.
The races are open to everyone, regardless of age and physical condition.

name: Håkøya Halvmaraton
description: Håkøya Half Marathon is a challenging course that starts at Storelva and goes to the end of the road on Håkøya. The race route is officially measured and consists mostly of asphalt, with some gravel, and is more hilly than a flat and fast course, but definitely offers opportunities for good times. This year, many debutants participated in the distance, who, with a solid training foundation, determination, and support from the club, crossed the finish line with smiles, well aware of having achieved a significant accomplishment.
course_highlights: A pack of debutants in the distance stood on the starting line for Northern Runners.
None of them had ever run that far, but most crossed the finish line smiling.
The course is beautiful, with a mix of asphalt and gravel, and offers opportunities to achieve good times.

name: Orkland Energimila
description: Orkanger IF invites all running enthusiasts to the Sports Park in Orkanger on Wednesday, August 13, for the 10th edition of the Orkland Energimila. The Energimila starts and finishes at the Athletics Track in the Sports Park and takes place on a flat and fast route in the center of Orkanger. The course is officially measured and approved by Kondis, with categories for both 5 km and 10 km for women and men. There will also be a children's race for the age group 0-12 years, with free registration and prizes for all participants.
course_highlights: The course is officially measured and approved by Kondis, and takes place on a flat and easily runnable loop in the center of Orkanger.
Children's race: 0-12 years - free registration and prizes for all participants.
Start time: 5 km at 6:00 PM and 10 km at 7:00 PM.

description: The Gloppe Trim is a 4 km long loop in Bukta that is great for walking, jogging, and running. We gather every week throughout the summer season (with a short break during the summer holidays). Those who wish to run with timing start at 7:00 PM. The Gloppe Trim is for everyone who wants to stay active, either on their own or together with others.
course_highlights: The Gloppetrimmen is a 4 km long loop trail in Bukta that is great for walking, jogging, and running.
We gather every week throughout the summer season (with a short break during the summer holidays).

name: Sommerkarusell Ålesund
description: The next and final race in the Ålesund Summer Carousel will take place on Wednesday, August 13, 2025, starting at 6:00 PM from the west end of Lillevatnet in Spjelkavik. The races begin at the parking lot by the walking path and head inland along Vasstranda on the southern side of Lillevatnet and Brusdalsvatnet. After 2.5 km and 5 km, the runners will turn around and run back to the start/finish line. There will be a joint start for the 5 km and 10 km precisely at 6:00 PM, and the courses are relatively flat with asphalt surfaces.

name: Geiteryggen 3k Barneløp
description: The Geiteryggen 3k Children's Race is for all children from the time they can run up until the year they turn 14. The courses mostly take place on trails, featuring both uphill and downhill sections, which makes it tiring but fun! Jumping in puddles is allowed, and the courses are well marked, so those who feel confident can run alone. The races are free, and registration can be done on-site up to 15 minutes before the start. Everyone receives a reusable race number, and at the finish line, juice and a medal await.
course_highlights: The trails mostly run on paths and include both uphill and downhill sections.
The races are free, and you can sign up by following the link below.

name: Ryggejoggen Løp
description: The Rygge Jog has never been cancelled - this is how they've kept it going for 35 years. This is the dream event for recreational runners, and the race has its season opening at the village museum in Rygge. Participants get the chance to experience an unforgettable run, just like Kristine Grønlie and her friends did when they encountered a sturdy wolf on the trail.
course_highlights: The Rygge Jog has never been canceled - that's how they've kept it going for 35 years.
The Rygge Jog: The dream offer for recreational runners.

name: Lustrafjorden Skyrace
description: Lustrafjorden Skyrace is a spectacular race that takes you through some of the most impressive landscapes in Norway. In 2026, we offer two distances: Lustrafjorden Inn – Ultra 100, from Kaupanger to Skjolden, approximately 104 km with 6000m of elevation gain, and Molden Skyrace, 22 km with 1270m of elevation gain, starting in Solvorn. This race is undoubtedly one of the most beautiful in Norway, but also one of the toughest, with a focus on all participants being winners, where the sense of achievement and the experience of nature are more important than the time. The event has an informal and social atmosphere, with a high enjoyment factor and a medal for everyone who finishes.
course_highlights: The course runs along the fjord and up into the mountains, where participants can experience breathtaking views of Lustrafjorden and the majestic mountains surrounding it.
The event places great emphasis on the fact that all participants are equally good winners, with the sense of achievement and the experience of nature being the most important.
The race is designed for both experienced runners and beginners, with varied terrain and challenges.

name: Stranda Fjord Trail Race
description: The Stranda Fjord Trail Race is a mountain and trail running event in the fjords of Norway, and is part of The Golden Trail Series. This race is known for its unique and challenging trails, featuring 25 kilometers of pure fjord trail bliss and 1800 meters of elevation gain and loss. The race starts with a 3-kilometer uphill stretch on gravel road, which is usually a good way to spread out the field. Runners experience a varied course with rocky and slippery sections, and can enjoy stunning views of the mountains and fjords.
course_highlights: The race attracts some of the best runners in the world, including Jonathan Albon and Sophia Laukli, who won the Golden Trail World Series.
Albon describes the race as unlike anything else in Europe, with varied trails and terrain.
There is a fantastic atmosphere among the participants, and the area has something truly magical about it.

name: Olsokløpet
description: The Olsokløpet took place on August 1 at Bønsnes Church, where Thomas Lundstad from Hytteplan sport won decisively with a time of 1:26:27. The race faced some challenges with wrong turns, as both Lundstad and last year's winner, Thomas Engenes, ran one kilometer too far. A total of 25 runners and cyclists participated, but only four women lined up at the start, with Ingunn Monsen being the fastest among them at 1:45:46. The organizers describe the course as Norway's most beautiful half marathon route and believe the race has the potential to grow in size.
course_highlights: Thomas Lundstad from Hytteplan Sport won decisively with a time of 1:26:27.
Ingunn Monsen was the fastest among the women with a time of 1:45:46.

There are several distances to choose from, including a children's race, 3.3 km, and 10 km, making it accessible for both beginners and experienced runners.
course_highlights: The start time for the children's race is 12:30, the 3.3 km starts at 13:00, and the 10 km starts at 14:00.

description: Langhusløpet 7th race is a free and fun running activity taking place on May 21 and June 24. There are two distances: 400 meters for children aged 0-7 years and 1,000 meters for children aged 8-12 years. Everyone who participates in both races before summer will receive a prize. Meeting time is at 5 PM at Langhushallen, where race numbers will be distributed before the start.

The 1,000 meters starts at the track and goes one lap up to the grass field, around, down again, and one lap around the main track in front of the Langhushallen.

name: Milæ
description: MILÆ is a flat city race held every year in Mosjøen, starting and finishing at Kippermoen stadium. Participants can choose between a competitive class or a fun run class without timing, and EVERYONE is welcome! You can take part in MILÆ 10 kilometers, Half 5 kilometers, FAMILY 5 kilometers, or a children's race of approximately 900 meters, also without timing. The course is designed for speed and excitement, with only 14 meters of elevation gain on the 5 km loop.
course_highlights: Participants can choose which type of race they want to enter, including 10 km, 5 km, and children's race.
The course is flat and has only 14 meters of elevation gain, making it one of Norway's fastest 5 and 10 km races.
Everyone is welcome, regardless of skill level, and both competitive and recreational classes are offered without timing.

This race challenges both endurance and strength, providing participants with a unique experience in scenic surroundings.

name: Sámi Maraton
description: Welcome to the northernmost marathon of mainland Norway! The Sámi Marathon takes place on August 16, 2025, in the Tanabru area, offering a marathon, half marathon, 10K, Run4fun 4.3K, and MiniMarathon. Participants can expect a varied and scenic course that takes them through the unique landscape of the Sámi region. The courses are accurately measured and certified, with special rounds for both young participants and para-athletes.
course_highlights: The marathon and half marathon have 2 and 4 laps respectively, while the 10K will be measured within this route.
Sámi Marathon is designed to provide participants with a beautiful nature experience through the unique landscape of the Sámi region.
There will be water stations along the courses, and race numbers can be picked up the day before the race or on race day.

name: Randaberg Backyard Ultra
description: Randaberg Backyard is designed as a social and inclusive race, where participants decide how many of the 12 laps they want to run, with the option to complete 50 miles / 80 km. Each lap starts on the hour, so it is important to develop a strategy that suits one's own pace. The faster you run, the longer break you get between laps. Between races, the Outdoor Life House serves as a break room where participants can relax and discuss the race with each other, creating a social and supportive atmosphere for the event.

The event offers a range of distances and a varied race, allowing both experienced runners and beginners to take part. The course is certified by Kondis 2022, and participants can expect a diverse route that goes through scenic areas, including walkways and forest trails.

The courses run through beautiful landscapes, and an emphasis is placed on an inclusive atmosphere for all participants.
Each stage has specific distances, and the routes take you through both urban and scenic landscapes.

This annual forest race gives participants the opportunity to experience scenic surroundings while competing.

name: Trysil-løpet
description: Welcome to the Trysil Race, a fast and flat race with minimal elevation gain! Participants can choose between distances of 10 km, 5 km, 600 m, and 300 m. In the 10 km, you'll have the chance to compete against well-known skiers like Petter Northug, Anders Aukland, and Hans Christer Holund. For the youngest participants, there are untimed races at 300 and 600 meters, where Petter joins the children. Everyone who finishes will receive a participation medal.

Welcome to challenge yourself against Petter Northug and Anders Aukland, who are participating in the 10 km.

name: Kårvatn Skyrace
description: Kårvatn is centrally located at the end of Todalen in Nordmøre, surrounded by beautiful, untouched nature. We want you to experience the joy of moving easily in the mountains! Sign up for one of the finest competitions of the fall, the Kårvatn Skyrace, which takes place on Saturday, August 17. Choose between the distances of 29 km - 1900 m elevation gain, 15 km - 1160 m elevation gain, 10 km - 750 m elevation gain, 4 km - 300 m elevation gain, or a Children's Race of 2.5 km. The start and finish are at Kårvatn, where there are also accommodation options for those who wish.
course_highlights: Choose between 29 km - 1900 m elevation gain, 15 km - 1160 m elevation gain, 10 km - 750 m elevation gain, 4 km - 300 m elevation gain, or a 2.5 km Kids' Course.
The course is marked all the way from start to finish.

name: Romerike Løpskarusell 6
description: Romerike Running Carousel is a running series with 8 different races spread across Romerike. Running is for everyone and is a social and enjoyable activity. You can choose whether you want to walk, jog, or run, with or without timing. Welcome! You can sign up for the entire running series or register for individual races.
course_highlights: Prize for everyone who completes 4 out of 8 races!
Running is for most people and is a social and enjoyable activity.

name: BDO-mila Skien
description: Welcome to BDO-Mila 2025 – our traditional race that brings together people of all ages and skill levels. This is a free event where you can choose whether to race for time or simply enjoy the journey at your own pace. BDO-Mila is the trail run that suits most participants and takes place in scenic surroundings. Participants can look forward to a well-organized course that is both challenging and fun, while the event emphasizes community and the joy of running.
course_highlights: All runners receive a free running shirt, and all children who run will get a medal.
The BDO Mile in Skien is a popular racing event that attracts participants of all ages.
Across the country, we create an arena every year where everyone can experience belonging and mastery through physical activity together with others.
