name: VABIK Terrengkarusell
description: The Terrain Carousel 2025 will be held on Wednesdays and Thursdays in Kristiansand, with marked trails and kilometer signs. The trails are marked from Wednesday at 1:00 PM to Thursday at 6:00 PM, and there is registration for completed times on Wednesday from 3:00 PM to 6:00 PM. On Thursday, there is a mass start for the short course at 5:30 PM, for the Milsluker at 5:00 PM (not for all races), and for the Children's Race at 5:10 PM (some races). To receive a participant prize, one must complete at least 8 races.
course_highlights: The courses are marked from Wednesday at 1:00 PM to Thursday at 6:00 PM.
Mass start short course at 5:30 PM and children's race at 5:10 PM (some races).
To receive a participant prize, you must complete at least 8 races.

name: Linnatrimmen
description: Linnatrimmen is a recreational race on Solbergfosslinna in Askim, with the start and finish at the Fire Station. The last edition of the spring season was held on June 5, and the next race will take place on August 21. Participants can choose between distances of 5 km and 2 km.
course_highlights: The Linnatrimmen is a recreational run on Solbergfosslinna in Askim, starting and finishing at the Fire Station.
The latest edition of the spring season was held on June 5th.
The next race will take place on August 21.

name: Sprek Elveløpet
description: Sprek Elveløpet is a certified (fitness) 5-kilometer street race that takes place every year in connection with Øras Dager in week 34. The course, which starts at Verdal Station, is flat and easy to run on asphalt and some firm gravel. This race is open to children, youth, adults, and families, and offers a wonderful walking and running experience along the picturesque River Promenade by the Verdalselva.
course_highlights: The course is flat and easy to run, mostly gravel as the surface, which is well-suited for both strollers and runners.
The result from the race will be approved for Norwegian statistics, which can be found at kondis.no/statistikk.
The race is organized in collaboration with Sprek Training Center and Verdal Athletics Club, and starts and ends on Jernbanegata.

name: Åsane Løpskarusell 5
description: Åsane Running Carousel 5 is a 5 km running competition organized by I.L. Norna-Salhus. The courses are measured by a certified course measurer from NFIF, with certification grade C, dated November 19, 2022, and valid until December 31, 2026. The race starts and finishes inside Ikea, with the start at 7:00 PM. Race numbers can be picked up in the garage at Ikea between 6:00 PM and 6:45 PM.
course_highlights: The courses have been officially measured by a certified course measurer from NFIF.
Start and finish inside Ikea (at the back of the building facing south).
5 km is officially measured on November 19, 2022.

name: Twilight 5000
description: Tracksmith Twilight 5000 is a series of races that offers a unique blend of competition and community. Runners take to the track under the floodlights and compete in the 5K distance on iconic tracks around the world. New York City, with its rich history and diverse communities, provides the perfect backdrop for the Twilight 5000 series, which takes place at Icahn Stadium along the East River. This race is a celebration of speed, endurance, and the vibrant communities that running creates.
course_highlights: Runners line up on the track beneath the floodlights and race the 5K distance at iconic venues around the world.
Dedicated pacers and like-minded competitors are there to keep you on pace, and the constant support of your local community carries you throughout the race.
At Bislett Stadium, runners will have the opportunity to compete on the same track as Olympians, surrounded by the city's iconic landmarks.

name: Ole Bull-løpet
description: The Ole Bull race takes place on Friday, September 16 at 7:00 PM (postponed from August 12) and is the 31st edition of the race. With fine conditions, clear and calm weather at +12, 77 participants took part. Emil Hosøy won the 6 km course with a time of 21:28, while the winners of the 4 km course were Bente R Midtun with 17:26 and Øystein Aamli with 13:31. The Ole Bull race is part of the running series by Osterøy IL/Athletics and takes place on scenic trails and roads in the area, providing participants the opportunity to experience beautiful landscapes while competing.
course_highlights: The Ole Bull race is part of the racing carousel of Osterøy IL/Athletics.
The race takes place on scenic trails and roads in the area.
Participants can choose between 4 km and 6 km distances.

name: Vossaton
description: Welcome to the whole family – for the children's race, 5 km, and half marathon in a spectacular course around Vangsvatnet, as well as the corporate relay. The half marathon and corporate relay start at 11:00 from Gjernes (1.5 km from the sports field), while the children's race starts at 11:10 at the sports field. The 5 km course has its start and finish at the sports field and goes through Prestegardsmoen. The courses are certified measured, and all participants will receive medals.
course_highlights: The half marathon and corporate relay start at 11:00 from Gjernes (1.5 km from the sports field).
The children's race starts at 11:10 AM and is a course of approximately 500 meters - on and around the sports field.
All participants receive medals, and there are prizes for the top three women and men.

name: Levanger Backyard
description: Levanger Ultrarunning Club, in collaboration with Intersport Magneten Levanger, invites you to Levanger Backyard 2025 on August 23 at 09:00. This event is a day filled with the joy of running, sore legs, a sense of achievement, and pleasant camaraderie. The concept is simple: runners must complete a lap of 6.7 km every hour, with new starts at the top of each hour. Participants can set their own goals, whether it’s to finish their first race event or to log up to 100.5 km by completing 15 laps.
course_highlights: There is a mass start every hour, so regardless of their goals, participants encounter the same people again at the start of the next round.
Everyone who completes a lap will receive a memento from the day, and there will be prize draws from local businesses.
The event includes music, food, coffee, and a great atmosphere in the finish area, as well as access to facilities at Nesset Community Center.

name: Den Breiale Milen
description: The Breiale Milen kicks off on August 17 in Frognerkilen, and this year the very successful event is being held on a Saturday. The race, which spans 14.50 km, starts and finishes at Kongen Marina, taking participants on a loop around Bygdøy and Sollerud beach. The event is known for its jovial atmosphere and includes a unique category for nose breathing, as well as a festive afterrun at Oslo's coolest venue.
course_highlights: The race has attracted both elite athletes and recreational runners, and the winner of the men's category, Eirik Aabrekk, set a new course record with a time of 49:19.
Tiril Knudsen, a skier in Norway's elite, won the women's category and expressed excitement about the relaxed atmosphere and the afterrun celebration.
The Breiale Mile is the only race with a separate category for nasal breathing (unisex), which adds an extra dimension and fun to the event.

name: Haglebu Backyard Ultra
description: Haglebu Backyard Ultra is an ultramarathon event taking place on August 23, 2025, with the start and finish at Haglebu Feriesenter. Participants must complete as many laps as possible of 6706 meters each hour, with a new lap starting every 60 minutes. There is a maximum of 12 laps, and the first man and woman to finish the last lap win the race. Everyone who completes at least one lap will receive a medal, and there will also be raffle prizes.
course_highlights: Medal for everyone who completes at least 1 lap.
1. prizes will be awarded to the best woman and man.
There will be a banquet at Haglebu Mountain Lodge after the race.

name: Drøbakløpet
description: The Drøbak Race replaces the traditional Blomstermila and has changed both the course layout and the start/finish location to Drøbak Torg. The race takes place in August, after the school year begins, to avoid competition with the end of school and vacation plans. The course runs from Drøbak Torg, through Kirkegata and Badeparken, past Drøbak Church, and ends up in Storgata. Parts of the course will be closed off to ensure traffic safety, but arrangements will be made for the town center to remain lively that afternoon.
course_highlights: The race starts at Drøbak Torg and follows a varied route that includes Badeparken, the fjord, and several well-known locations in Drøbak.
The race is scheduled for August 24, which allows for participation after the start of school.
Previous pre-runs have shown that the course layout is popular, with participants both big and small cheering for each other.

name: Tromsø Mountain Ultra 50km
description: The Tromsø Mountain Ultra 50 km is part of the Tromsø Mountain Challenge, which has something for everyone, from Dalheim Rundt to the La Sportiva Half Ultra. The ultramarathon starts at Snarbyeidet and concludes with a spectacular descent through beautiful Tromsdalen, finishing at TUIL Arena. The race takes place in varied and hilly terrain that offers approximately 1700 meters of elevation gain to tackle, with trails that test strength and endurance, as well as views that inspire – an adventure that attracts runners from all over the world.
course_highlights: The ultramarathon of 50 km starts from Snarbyeidet, while the half-ultramarathon (25 km) starts from TUIL Arena.
Both races conclude with a spectacular descent through beautiful Tromsdalen and finish at TUIL Arena.
The race takes place in varied and hilly terrain, offering approximately 1700 meters of elevation gain to contend with.

name: HalvUltra 25km
description: The half-ultramarathon (25 km) starts from TUIL Arena and concludes with a spectacular descent through the beautiful Tromsdalen, finishing back at TUIL Arena. No matter which race you choose, you'll encounter trails that test strength and endurance, and views that inspire – an adventure that attracts runners from all over the world.
course_highlights: The race concludes with a spectacular descent through beautiful Tromsdalen.
The finish line is back at TUIL Arena.

name: Kystleden Halvmaraton
description: The Kystleden Half Marathon starts at Linden Senter in Horten, about 80 meters south of the ticket office for the Bastøferga. The course follows the coastal path along the water, with a turnaround at the kiosk on Steinbrygga, before taking you out of the woods by the treatment plant and back to Horten via the coastal path. This race offers you the chance to experience stunning natural scenery while challenging yourself in a half marathon.
course_highlights: Start at Linden Center in Horten (approximately 80 m south of the ticket booth for Bastøferga).
Coastal path along the water with a turn at the kiosk by Steinbrygga.

description: On Saturday, the starting gun was fired for the very first time for the Stavekollen Sky Run, organized by Ikornnes IL. This exciting race takes place in Sykkylven, Møre og Romsdal, Norway.
course_highlights: Stavekollen Sky Run is the first race of its kind in the area.
The event is organized by Ikornnes IL.
The race takes place in beautiful surroundings in Møre and Romsdal.

name: Vikerfjell Challenge
description: Vikerfjell Challenge is an exciting running experience with fantastic nature encounters and challenging courses. Participants can choose between three distances: 21 km, 11 km, and a 2.5 km children's race. The courses run on gravel roads, trails, and in terrain, so be prepared to get your feet wet. The longest distance starts from Ringerudsetra and ends at Skarrudsetra, while the 11 km course starts from Tossviksetra.
course_highlights: Fantastic nature, atmosphere, and trails – take the challenge!
The course runs on gravel roads, trails, and in terrain, so be prepared to get your feet wet.
First 10 km mainly on gravel road, then 8 km on trail and terrain before the last 3 km is mostly on gravel road.

name: Nipkollen Challenge
description: The Nipkollen Challenge is not just any race – it’s a raw experience through Nannestad's most beautiful and challenging terrain. This is not about fast asphalt kilometers, but about mastering technical trails, steep ascents, and undulating stretches that truly test you. Three distances – one common challenge: 14 km for all ages, 25 km for the tough, and 50 km for the truly dedicated, which is one of Norway's toughest ultramarathons. The race offers participants the chance to test their skills in a spectacular setting, with views that reward the effort.
course_highlights: 14 km – Perfect for those who want to experience the magic of trail running. Open to all ages!
25 km – A solid challenge for the tough. Age limit 14 years.
50 km – Ultra for the truly dedicated! This is one of Norway's toughest ultra distances, and we promise you'll feel it in both your legs and your mind. Age limit 16 years.

name: Ulvøyløpet
description: The Ulvøyløpet is a trail run that crosses the mountain from Stokmarknes to Melbu, where everyone can participate. It is being held for the ninth time and offers participants the chance to enjoy a nice trip over the mountain or compete in either a long or short course. The event takes place on Saturday, August 23, 2025, with a recreational start from 9:30 AM to 11:30 AM and competitive classes starting at 12:00 PM. Both courses begin at Hadselhallen in Stokmarknes and finish at the community center in Melbu, with distances of approximately 10 km and under 25 km.
course_highlights: There will be a bonfire and sticks for grilling sausages at the drink station by Sorgenfri.
The long course is changing in 2024 based on feedback from runners, and is now just under 25 km with almost 900 meters of elevation gain.
There will be a café at Melbu by the finish line.

images.alt_text: Map of the route from Stokmarknes to Melbu.

name: Trondheim Maraton
description: The Trondheim Marathon course encircles the city center of Trondheim, and our goal is to showcase the city in a beautiful way. Participants will experience much of what Trondheim has to offer in terms of both history and culture. The course is certified and AIMS-approved, with a distance of 10.5 km. Half marathon runners will complete 2 laps, while full marathon runners will do 4 laps, making it easy for the cheering crowd to see the participants multiple times — very spectator-friendly!
course_highlights: The course is officially measured and AIMS-certified (TrøndelagKraft 5ern, BDO-MILA, Brilliant half marathon and full marathon).
The course runs through the heart of Trondheim city center, providing participants with a unique experience of the city's history and culture.
We also have a mini-marathon for children, which makes the event inclusive for the whole family.

name: Børløpet
description: Støren Ski is pleased to invite you to Børløpet, a street race in Støren Center. The start and finish are at Gauldalsporten, with a children's race for those aged 3-12 starting at 11:30, followed by the competition starting at 12:15. Participants in the fitness class will start individually between 11:00 and 12:00. The children's race is 1 km and free to enter, while the fitness class is 5 km with an entry fee of 50,-. The 5 km competition will award prizes to the top three in the women's and men's categories.
course_highlights: Children's race 1km: Registration on race day. Prize for everyone, sponsored by KIWI Støren. Free participation.
5km Fun Run: Registration on race day. Entry fee 50,-.
Competition 5km: Prizes for 1st, 2nd, and 3rd in the women's/men's category. Entry fee 180,- including license.

name: Østmarka Trail Challenge
description: Østmarka Trail Challenge – The Refugee Route is a tough trail race of about 37 km that follows blue-marked paths through Østmarka. The course follows a route that was used during World War II to help people escape the country, and runs between Enebakk/Øyeren and Skullerud in Oslo. This race is incredibly fun and challenging, providing participants with a unique experience in scenic surroundings.
course_highlights: The course follows a route that was used during World War II to smuggle people out of the country.
Østmarka Trail Challenge organizes tough and challenging trail races in Østmarka.
Participants will have the opportunity to try to claim the title of "Queen of Bruises."

name: Vegabølgen
description: The Vegabølgen race offers several distances, including 3 km, 5 km, 10 km, and half marathon. The route for the 10 km starts at the school and goes via Nessjøen intersection, Andvågan, Færset, Åsen, the entrance to the Health House, before finishing in front of the grandstand on the artificial turf field. The half marathon begins at Sundsvoll and includes a scenic route down to Vallsjø and back up to Valla again, before concluding on the artificial turf field. The children's race will take place on the artificial turf field.
course_highlights: The 10 km route will be: Start at the school – Nessjøen intersection – Andvågan – Færset – Åsen – entrance to the Health House – artificial turf field – finish line in front of the stands at the artificial turf field.

The route for the half marathon will be: Start at Sundsvoll – down to Vallsjø and back up to Valla – towards Gladstad – take the love path down to Kirkøy – Nes – around Syveien – towards Gladstad – Nesjøen intersection towards the school – the entrance to the health center – the artificial turf field – finish line in front of the grandstand at the artificial turf field.

The 3 km route will be: Start at the entrance to the Health House – Nessjøen intersection – Burshaugen (the entrance to the municipal building) – the path to Kolstadsjøen – Kolstad – Nessjøen intersection – finish line in front of the grandstand on the artificial turf field.

name: Skåbu Fjellmaraton Ultra
description: Skåbu Fjellmaraton Ultra starts at Bygdin on Valdresflya, about 13 km from Beitostølen, and follows the Jotunheim Road past idyllic mountain farms along Vinstervatna. The race offers fantastic views of the peaks of Jotunheimen and beautiful mountains. From about 35 km, participants follow the marathon course all the way to the finish, with a tough ending up the notorious Kamfossbakken, which has an average incline of 10% over 3 km. This race takes place in the foothills of Jotunheimen and includes an incorporated uphill race.
course_highlights: The race follows the Jotunheim Road past idyllic mountain farms along Vinstervatna on gravel roads.
Fantastic view of the peaks of Jotunheimen and beautiful mountains.
The finale of the three longest races is the notorious Kamfossbakken, with its 2.5 km and an average incline of 10%.

Participants will experience a varied route with both gravel roads and trails, as well as stunning views of the sea. The race is suitable for both beginners and experienced runners, and there are several distances to choose from.
course_highlights: The Coastal Trail Around takes you through beautiful coastal areas in Bud, Møre and Romsdal.
Participants will experience a varied course with both gravel roads and trails.

name: Tromsø Mountain Challenge
description: Tromsø Mountain Challenge is a weekend with four trail races over three days in Tromsø, offering a total of five races, including the Ultra 50K and TMC Half Ultra 25K. The event takes place in the beautiful nature surrounding Tromsø, featuring spectacular views and challenging terrain. Runners have the opportunity to experience the midnight sun while navigating through varied trails and mountainous areas.
course_highlights: The northern Norwegian mountains offer great contrasts with runnable terrain, steep slopes, and a beautiful view of the fjord.
Two uphill races are offered, including a relay, an ultramarathon, and two trail runs.
The Tromsø Mountain Challenge has achieved an impressive victory in its debut year, setting a record in the new course.

name: Strandvoldrunden
description: Race veteran Arne Moren (72) feels the nerves ahead of the first Strandvoldrunde in 25 years. Not for his own sake, but because he fears that not enough officials will show up. This is the first edition of the Strandvoldrunde since the collapse in 1993, and Moren is among the ten to twelve pre-registered runners hoping to complete the nine-kilometer course in under an hour.
course_highlights: The 72-year-old is among those who have taken on the toughest challenges ahead of this year's edition of the Strandvoldrunden.
Emil Fallet, 14 years old, was the one who ran the fastest in this year's Strandvoldrunde.
This is the first Strandvold round since the user collapse in 1993.

name: Mandalsmaraton
description: The Mandalsmarathon was first held in 1980 and is one of Norway's oldest marathons. The southernmost marathon in Norway is now back in a new guise with a course close to the city center in particularly picturesque surroundings. The route takes you through the charming streets of Mandal's center and Furulunden, known for its beautiful nature and idyllic beaches. The Mandalsmarathon aims to be a race for everyone, whether it's your first race or you're chasing a new personal record. Everyone is welcome here – whether you run, jog, or walk.
course_highlights: The course takes you through Mandal's charming downtown streets and Furulunden, known for its beautiful nature and idyllic beaches.
Along the course, you are greeted by life and activity, music, and an engaged audience that contributes to an unforgettable racing experience.
Mandalsmarathon aims to be a race for everyone, whether it's your first race or you're chasing a new personal record.

Spread over two days in Tromsø's unique mountain landscape.

description: The Mandalsmarathon was first held in 1980 and is one of Norway's oldest marathons. The southernmost marathon in Norway is now back in a new guise with a course close to the city center in particularly picturesque surroundings. The route takes you through the charming streets of Mandal's center and Furulunden, known for its beautiful nature and idyllic beaches. name: Hornindalsrokken Skyrace
description: The Hornindalsrokken Skyrace is a new race in 2026, aimed at experienced mountain runners. The course is approximately 17.5 km long with around 1300 meters of elevation gain, taking you through beautiful western Norwegian nature with turquoise lakes, steep mountain slopes, and spectacular views from Hornindalsrokken (1,526 m above sea level). The highlight is the challenging ascent up Rokkeråsa – 1.3 km with 506 meters of elevation gain and technical terrain. After reaching the summit, a airy ridge awaits, followed by a thrilling descent towards Kjellstaddalen.

name: Halddemarsjen
description: The Halddemarsjen is a traditional hiking march and uphill race that takes place annually at the end of August. The march starts in Kåfjord, 15 km south of Alta, and goes up to the now-closed northern lights observatory at Halddetoppen, 907 meters above sea level. Participants can choose between a hiking class and a competition class, and the march follows a relatively good cart road to the top, about 9 km. The average incline is 10%, but in the last kilometer, it rises by 20%, and hikers should plan for a minimum of 2-3 hours for the ascent.

name: Mud Monkey 2025
description:
MUDMONKEY 2025

Welcome to the Jungle. Play Dirty. Laugh Louder.

Mud. Obstacles. Screams and laughter. This is not a race – this is the jungle's playground for adults (and teenagers who aren't afraid to slip in style).

MudMonkey 2025 invites you to a day of total bananas in nature: climbing, crawling, water, fire, and a bunch of race-crazy Monkeys who live to challenge you through the course. Forget asphalt and fences – here you face the jungle's resistance with a grin.

MUDMONKEY 5K – “Monkey Business in Battle Mode”

5 kilometers with 25 technical and natural obstacles. 
You climb, tumble, crawl, and laugh your way through the mud while unruly MudMonkeys try to block you – physically. 
Go solo or as a tribe – but one thing is for sure: You will emerge covered in mud and full of adrenaline.

Age limit: 13+

A parental declaration must be signed before the start (sent via email the week before the race).

MUDMONKEY 8K – “Mud Mayhem and Jungle Fury”

8 kilometers. 40+ obstacles.

When you think it can't get wilder, you arrive here. 
This is the highlight of the obstacle race: mud pits, zip lines, icy water, flames, slippery stones – and of course, crazy MudMonkeys trying to topple you with laughter and resistance.

Age limit: 16+

A declaration must be signed before the start (sent via email the week before the race).

____________________________________________________________________________________

COMING 2026 – MUDMONKEY EXTREME 21K

“For those who have never been dirty enough”

21 km. 70+ obstacles. Here you will meet your limits – and have them shattered.

Spectator-friendly, but participant-hostile course full of fire, ice, mud, and monkey madness.

Only for the most bananas among us.

Age limit: 18+
A declaration must be signed before the start (sent via email the week before the race).

EVERYONE GETS A MEDAL – NO ONE GOES HOME DRY OR CLEAN!!

Here, competition is held in individual classes and in tribes (teams). 
The fastest will be celebrated with honor and glory – but everyone who finishes gets a medal and the right to call themselves a true MudMonkey.
additional: Feel free to call us at 95961803 or send an email to hei@xchallenge.no.

name: Averøy 3 Fjell
description: Averøy 3 Fjell is a beautiful mountain race that takes place right at the edge of the sea near the Atlantic Road. It consists of three stunning mountain peaks: Gulltanna, Fagerfjellet, and Meekknoken. The race is 18 km long with 1200 meters of elevation gain, and in the competitive and recreational categories, participants must visit all the peaks, while the leisure class allows for choosing how many of them to visit. Additionally, there is a hike for children up to Skårrå, which is 2.5 km one way.
course_highlights: The race passes through the peaks of Gulltanna, Fagerfjellet, and Meekknoken.
The start and finish are at Mork Stadium, and the race is organized by Averøy Running Club.
Next year's race will be held on August 31, 2024.

name: Lyderhorn Opp
description: Lyderhorn Opp is a combination of a social outdoor event for the whole family, an informal fun run, and a mountain running competition. The starting point is at Falck Nutec in Gravdal, with the finish line at the top of Lyderhorn, 396 meters above sea level. The course is approximately 3.8 km, and all school students in the Laksevåg district are offered the opportunity to participate for free.
course_highlights: Lyderhorn Opp is a social outdoor event for the whole family.
The starting point is at Falck Nutec in Gravdal, with the finish line at the top of Lyderhorn, 396 meters above sea level.
All school students in the Laksevåg district are offered the opportunity to participate for free.

name: Ragnarok OCR
description: Ragnarok OCR is an obstacle race that will test your physical and mental limits, and is being organized in connection with the 10th anniversary of Achievers Multisport Team. The race takes place on September 28th in Bygnes, Karmøy, and has a Norse mythology theme. There will be an adult race, a family race, and a children's race, and the event is designed to be accessible for everyone, from beginners to elite athletes. Corporate teams, sports clubs, and bachelor parties can also register.
course_highlights: The race has a Norse mythology theme.
There will be an adult race, a family race, and a children's race.
Everyone should be able to participate, whether they are completely untrained or an elite athlete.

name: Førde Opp
description: The Bystien Førde Opp is a mountain race that ascends the Bystien trail in Hafstadkleiva on Hafstadfjellet in Førde in Sunnfjord. In this year's race, Ane Brekke from Førde IL Friidrett won the women's category with a time of 37:28, while Geir Steig from Luster IL took victory in the men's category with a time of 28:12. The race gathered around 1,000 participants.
course_highlights: Bystien Førde Opp – uphill race on the city trail up Hafstadkleiva on Hafstadfjellet in Førde in Sunnfjord.
Ane Brekke from Førde IL Athletics (time: 37:28) and Geir Steig from Luster IL (time: 28:12) won the women's and men's categories in this year's mountain race.
There were about 1,000 participants this year.

name: Dogrun Ridderdagene
description: Vom Dogrun is for everyone who wants to join in a pleasant activity with their dog. You can choose to participate with or without timing, and it’s a social and fun outing with your dog, in the company of other dog lovers. VOM PUPPY WALK is a separate activity for puppies – which is free to sign up for. Additionally, Vom Dogrun is free for all participants under 18 years old, and every participant receives a medal.
course_highlights: VOM PUPPY WALK is a special activity for puppies – which is free to sign up for.
The Vom Dogrun is free for everyone under 18 years old.
There is a participation medal for everyone.

name: HOKA-mila Moelv
description: The HOKA Mile is a 10,000-meter track race held on the new blue track in Moelv, Skarpsno Arena, on Saturday, August 31. This race is for everyone, and participants are divided into heats based on their expected finish times, providing a golden opportunity for fast times, whether you are chasing a personal record or the national championship requirement. With 25 flat laps without a single meter of elevation, the organizers promise a fantastic day dedicated to running and community, with a great atmosphere and festive surroundings.
course_highlights: The HOKA Mile is held on the new blue track in Moelv, Skarpsno Arena, and is a race for everyone, with heats tailored to "your" pace.
This race is a golden opportunity for fast times, whether you run the 10K in just over an hour or under half an hour.
The organizers promise a great atmosphere and a festive environment around this new, audience-friendly race.

name: Ogndalsløpet
description: The Ogndalsløpet was held on a warm and pleasant evening at Ogndal School on Thursday, June 13, where course records were set for both women and men. The event attracted nearly 100 participants, who could also take part in the children's race and a non-timed fitness run.
course_highlights: Course records were set for both women and men in the Ogndalsløpet.
The event took place at Ogndal School.
Almost 100 participants lined up at the starting line.

name: Hessjøen Rundt
description: Hessjøen Rundt is a race featuring a recreational course. The course for the competitive class and the longest recreational route is approximately 12 km long, while the recreational course is about 6 km with a relatively flat profile, suitable for the whole family. The race takes place on Saturday, August 31, 2024, with the start and finish at Stevneplassen. Participants can register from 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM for the recreational class, while the competitive classes start at 12:00 PM.
course_highlights: Everyone receives a participant badge, and the top three in each competition class are rewarded with gift cards.
There is a kiosk at the start and finish area that sells coffee, soda, hamburgers, hot dogs, cake, and more.
To drive on Hessjøvegen, one must pay a fee of 70 NOK.

name: Hardangervidda Marathon
description: Welcome to the Dynafit Hardangervidda Marathon! This is not an ordinary marathon where you run on asphalt in a flat course profile. Here, the keywords are mountain plateaus and grand nature experiences. You will run in mountain terrain in spectacular surroundings on Hardangervidda, with two grueling climbs that are guaranteed to burn. On this day, you will use all your strength and experience a nature adventure you will not soon forget.
course_highlights: You run in mountainous terrain in spectacular surroundings on the Hardangervidda.
The course has both technically demanding sections and nice fast trails.
An enthusiastic crew will cheer you on, and you might need that.

Running in the Hardangervidda marathon. Beautiful, but challenging terrain.

name: Molde Maraton
description: Molde Marathon is an annual running festival in Molde, Møre og Romsdal, bringing together both recreational runners and competitive athletes. The event offers several distances, including a full marathon, half marathon, 10 km, 5 km, and child-friendly races. The race is known for its scenic route along Fannefjorden, featuring spectacular views of the majestic Romsdal Alps. Molde Marathon is held twice a year – as a spring race in April and an autumn race in August.
course_highlights: The event offers several distances, including a full marathon, half marathon, 10 km, 5 km, and child-friendly races.
The race is known for its scenic route along Fannefjorden, with spectacular views of the majestic Romsdal Alps.
The Molde Marathon is held twice a year – as a spring race in April and a fall race in August.

name: Lofoten High5 Svolvær
description: Lofoten High5 is a spectacular mountain running race based on five peaks that can all be seen from Svolvær square. The peaks are Fløya (590 m), Blåtind (621 m), Tuva (477 m), Lille Kongstind (378 m), and Tjeldbergtind (367 m), and the views from all five summits are magical. No climbing gear is needed, but parts of the route, especially Fløya and Blåtind, involve steep and challenging terrain. All proceeds are used to support the development and maintenance of the trail.
course_highlights: Lofoten High5 has contributed funds to the sherpa staircase.
You can choose between four activities: High5 Competition, High5 Hiking, and High3 Competition.
High5 Competition has its own men's and women's categories with timing and an estimated finish time under 5.5 hours.

name: Vardeløpet Sula Fjelløp
description: The Vardeløpet is a mountain race that goes from the Devold factory in Langevåg to the finish line at Vonhytta at 510 meters above sea level. The course length is 4.5 km, with a competitive class that includes timing. This year, more emphasis is placed on recreational runners and families, with great prizes drawn from the start numbers. The organizer promises fun activities along the route and an exciting journey from the foot of the mountain to Vonhytta, where you might encounter familiar fairy tale characters.
course_highlights: There will be a competitive class with timekeeping as before.
This year, the Vardeløpet will be more family-oriented, with nice prizes drawn from the bib numbers.
There will be fun activities throughout the Vonløypa and upon arrival at Vonhytta.

name: Tåsentiern
description: The Tåsentiern is a race that takes you through beautiful scenic spots in Oslo. The courses are varied and suited for both beginners and experienced runners, creating a great atmosphere and the opportunity to explore the fantastic surroundings. This race is an excellent chance to experience nature while you train.
course_highlights: The courses are varied and tailored for both beginners and experienced runners.
Participants can look forward to a great atmosphere.
The opportunity to explore the amazing surroundings.

name: Porsgrunn Halvmaraton
description: Experience the news of the Porsgrunn Half Marathon 2025, a community celebration in Porsgrunn City Center. The start and finish line is at Franklintorget outside the Down Town shopping center, where there will also be entertainment, booths, and a free children's race. The Porsgrunn Half Marathon is an accessible race for everyone, regardless of skill level, and there is the option to participate alone or with family, friends, and colleagues. We look forward to creating an unforgettable community celebration for both runners and spectators!
course_highlights: There will be entertainment and a great atmosphere along the course for both runners and spectators.
Participate alone or with family, friends, and colleagues and have fun together.
Over 1500 children and adults participated in 2025, and we look forward to a new community celebration.

name: Grensetrimmen
description: The Grensetrimmen is a recreational race that takes place on runner-friendly trails and gravel roads, with some asphalt sections on the Swedish side. The course features a few moderate inclines in the middle section but is relatively flat and easy to run. The distance is stated to be 10 km (but was measured at 9.3 km) and has remained the same since its inception in 1983. The race takes place on the first Saturday in September at Støa in Trysil.
course_highlights: The course has some moderate inclines in the middle section, but is relatively flat and easy to run.
The distance is stated as 10 km (but was measured at 9.3 km).
The Border Trim has been organized since 1983.

name: Kolbotnvannet Rundt
description: Kolbotnvannet Rundt features a course in scenic surroundings on terrain, gravel, and asphalt. You can participate with or without timing, with distances of 5 km and 10 km. The start is at Kolbotn Torg, and the route includes asphalt, forest trails, and gravel, with a finish line after 5 km. There is also a family event with a shorter loop of about 2 km, perfect for strollers.
course_highlights: Race with timing: Compete for the best possible time, with course lengths of 5 km and 10 km (two laps).
Run without timing: Complete at your own pace and enjoy the surroundings around Kolbotnvannet.
We also have a family event in the vicinity of Kolbotn Torg, with competitions along the route.

name: Styrkeprøven Rett Vest
description: Styrkeprøven Rett Vest is an ultramarathon held in the mountains of Bergen on the last weekend of August. The course, which stretches approximately 45 km from Gullbotn to Kjøkkelvik, has a total elevation gain of over 3000 meters and includes several peaks such as Gullfjellstoppen and Ulriken. Since its inception in 1984, this event has become an annual tradition for many running enthusiasts, with course records of 4 hours and 40 minutes for men and 6 hours and 3 minutes for women. In 2023, Styrkeprøven Rett Vest celebrated its 35th anniversary.
course_highlights: The route starts at Gullbotn and ascends to the summit of Gullfjell, which is the highest point of the route at 987 meters.
The course has a total elevation gain of over 3000 meters, providing a challenging and scenic experience.
Styrkeprøven Rett Vest is composed of volunteer members focused on creating a healthy and motivating activity event.

name: Ledenløpet Fåvang-Øyer
description: The Ledenløpet 2025 is a race through the cultural landscape in the heart of Gudbrandsdalen. Four distances are offered: Long Trail 27 km (Black), Middle Trail 17 km (Red), Short Trail 7 km (Blue), and Raspberry Trail 1 km. All distances finish at Nermo Hotel, and the race follows the Pilgrims' Trail from Fjøssystemer (Sør-Fåvang) to Øyer.
course_highlights: The Leden Race 2025 is a race through the cultural landscape in the heart of Gudbrandsdalen.
Four distances are offered: Long Trail 27 km (Black), Medium Trail 17 km (Red), Short Trail 7 km (Blue), and Raspberry Trail 1 km.
All distances finish at Nermo Hotel.

name: Hodlekve Fjelløp
description: Join the mountain race of a lifetime! Hodlekve Rundt takes place on Saturday, September 24, and offers distances of 21 km, 10 km, and 6 km in beautiful terrain. This is the fourth year the race is being organized, and the routes follow marked trails. The activity day in Hodlekve will have offerings for both young and old, with a junior race, a treasure hunt, and sales of coffee and food at Dalalåven, which is open from 10:00 AM to 3:00 PM.
course_highlights: The starting gun for the 21 km race goes off at 10:00, while the 10 km and 6 km races start at 10:30.
Dalalåven will have open coffee with food and drink service, as well as bike rental available on this day.
There will be activities for the whole family, including a junior race and a treasure hunt from Sognenett.

name: Oslo Løpsfestival - Fornebu Rundt
description: The Oslo Running Festival consists of eight races along the capital's beautiful trails and scenic roads. You can run whenever you want – alone or together with others, either in the SOLO category or in the team competition as a DUO or TRIO. Each race is announced on Friday at 12:00, and the course is open until Sunday at 11:00 the following weekend, with a mass start precisely at 11:00. The course is certified to be as close to 10 km as possible.
course_highlights: You can participate alone in the SOLO class, or in the team competition as a DUO or TRIO.
Each race is scheduled to be announced on Friday at 12:00 PM, and the course is open until Sunday at 11:00 AM the following weekend.
The course has been officially measured to be as close to 10 km as possible.

name: Vassfjellet Rundt
description: Welcome to the 56th edition of Vassfjellet Rundt on Sunday, August 31, 2025. This is the race for everyone, whether you want to compete for time, spend the day hiking in the mountains, or visit the Vassfjelltroll in the Trolløypa. The course runs on gravel roads, forest roads, trails, and in terrain, with the start and finish at Tanem School. Three course distances are offered: a stroller-friendly Troll course of 3 km, a short course of about 13 km for juniors, recruits, and veterans aged 60 and over, as well as a long course of about 18 km for senior men and women.
course_highlights: Troll trail (Stroller-friendly): 3km.
Short course approximately 13 km (Junior/recruit/veteran from 60 years competition).
Long course approximately 18 km (Men and women senior competition).

name: Klempheia Rundt
description: Klempheia Rundt is an approximately 10/12 km recreational run that will take place on Sunday, August 25, 2024, at 9:30 AM, starting and finishing at Hemne Ski Center. This is the 47th edition of the race, and we encourage everyone to register in advance, although there will be opportunities for late registration upon arrival. Participants can look forward to a wonderful round trip in the woods, with the chance to meet friendly people along the way.
course_highlights: The course is varied and challenging, with gravel roads, trails, marshes, mountains, and tractor paths.
The recreational class is 10 kilometers, while competitive runners over 16 years old must run 12 kilometers, including an extra loop around the ski center.
The event has been the club's largest for many years and has a long tradition in Kyrksæterøra.

images.alt_text: Runner on the road in the landscape.

name: Røykenmila
description: The Røykenmila is a race that aims to create value in the local community and serves as an activity day for the whole family. The event has three goals: to create a festive day for everyone together with businesses and local associations, to motivate people to start training, and to raise money for good causes in the local community. There is an inclusive atmosphere with awards for participants in the 5 km and 10 km distances, as well as activities, booths, and entertainment for the entire family.
course_highlights: Røykenmila aims to create value in the local community and motivate people to start training.
The event includes activities for the whole family, with booths and entertainment.
There is an inclusive atmosphere with awards for participants in the 5 km and 10 km distances.

name: Klev Opp Angers
description: Klev Opp Angers starts from Sandebukta by Bogen and goes up to the plateau at Kleiverud. The name comes from the old name for Sandebukta, Sande Alpinklubb. The hike from Bogen to the top of Angers klev offers little to no view, but provides a historical experience of the old cart road. At the top, one can stroll to a viewpoint behind the antenna mast, where there is a fantastic view over the fjord and Løvøya.
course_highlights: At Bogen, there is a parking lot with space for quite a few cars.
Although the trail offers little in terms of views along the way, the journey holds more historical value than a hiking experience.
A large part of the route is on a trail with rough stones, so it is recommended to wear hiking shoes or sturdy running shoes.

name: Puttekollen Opp
description: Puttekollen Opp is a family-friendly summit hike in Begnadalen with a great view towards Sørum. The trail goes through easy forest terrain and is approximately 1.5 km one way, with an elevation gain of about 200 meters. It takes about 45−60 minutes to complete and is suitable for children from around 5 years old.
course_highlights: Family-friendly summit hike in Begnadalen with a nice view towards Sørum.
The route goes through easy forest terrain.
Suitable for children from about 5 years old.

name: Norgestesten
description: The Norgestest is organized by volunteers from the Jessheim Running Group and Ull/Kisa Athletics, with proceeds going towards sports for children and youth. The race takes place in Jessheim with a mass start, featuring a flat course of 3,146 meters. Participants can choose between distances ranging from 3 km to half marathon, including a fantastic children's race of 800 meters. The event has simple logistics, with parking and restrooms located 300 meters from the start, and self-service bib number pickup.
course_highlights: The race takes place on Sundays at 10:00 AM to make the execution as efficient as possible.
All distances start the same, which gives participants the opportunity to run alongside many others.
Participants receive a well-deserved medal after the race.

name: Sørlandstesten Løp 1
description: The Sørlandstest is a new low-threshold offer for happy recreational runners of all levels. The start and finish are located across the road from Gumpens Auto, along Setesdalsveien in Kristiansand. Participants follow a flat and fast course up Setesdalsveien to Strai, turn around, and run back the same way. If you're running 5 km, you turn around after passing 2.5 km. The course is officially measured, and the race is approved by and listed on NFIF's official schedule.
course_highlights: The start and finish are on the other side of the road from Gumpens Auto, along Setesdalsveien in Kristiansand.
The participants follow a flat and fast course up Setesdalsveien to Strai, turn around, and run back the same way.
The course has been officially measured and the race is approved by and listed on NFIF's official calendar.

name: Flemstubben
description: The Flemstubben race is an annual road race held in Flemma, and this year it was conducted for the 44th time with 140 participants. The race has a distance of 10 kilometers, and Johan Bugge from Eidsvåg IL was the pre-race favorite, delivering a time of 30:52, just 6 seconds behind his own course record. Live Johannessen Solheimdal from Steinkjer FIK smashed her own record with an impressive time of 34:41, while Morten Eilifsen from Averøy Running Club achieved the second-best overall time with 34:35.
course_highlights: Johan Bugge from Eidsvåg IL lived up to his status as the favorite with a time of 30:52, just 6 seconds behind his own course record.
Live Johannessen Solheimdal smashed her own course record with a time of 34:41, an improvement of nearly one and a half minutes.
Morten Eilifsen achieved the second-best overall time with 34:35 and won the M40-49 category.

name: Arnaløpet
description: Welcome to the Arnaløpet 2025, taking place on Monday, August 25th at Espeland Sports Ground. The family race of 3.4 km starts at 19:00 and is free for children born in 2013 and later. The Arnaløpet 10 km starts at 19:30, with individual registrations costing 200 NOK (+ license). The registration deadline for both family and individual entries is at 18:30 on the same day.

The family price for up to five people is 600 NOK (+ license), and everyone can bring a friend.

Participants can challenge themselves in Race 1: 5 Km Bingen Loop, Race 2: 9 Km Aasgaard Loop, Race 3: 6 Km Light Trail, and Race 4: 800m Track. This event provides a great opportunity for both experienced runners and beginners to participate in different distances.

name: GT-Karusellen Løp
description: The GT Carousel is a fun run for both young and old, organized by the clubs Vind IL, Gjøvik Skiklub, ØTS, and Raufoss at their various venues throughout the year. The courses take place in beautiful surroundings on the clubs' trail routes and have distances ranging from 1 km to 9 km. The routes are well marked, and there are categories with and without timing, so everyone can participate. This year, parents are especially encouraged to join in to restore the large starting field and the shared joy of running.
course_highlights: The courses take place in beautiful surroundings on the clubs' trail routes and have distances ranging from 1 km to 9 km.
There are classes with and without timing, so everyone who wants to can participate.
This year, we especially encourage parents to participate so that we can bring back the large starting field and the shared joy of running.

name: Midtåsenløpet
description: Welcome to the 12th edition of the Midtåsen Race on Wednesday, September 11, 2024. This is Sandefjord's own uphill race with a finish at the historic Midtåsen – a perfectly challenging event that everyone can manage! The course is 2480 m with a total elevation gain of 110 m, starting at Sandefjord Tinghus at 18:30 for participants aged 16 and younger, and at 18:40 for participants aged 17 and older. There will also be a separate children's race starting at 18:00 from Mokollen Barnehage.
course_highlights: The course is 2480 m with a total elevation gain of 110 m.
Start at Sandefjord Courthouse at 6:30 PM (16 years and younger) and 6:40 PM (17 years and older).
Separate children's race starting at 6:00 PM from Mokollen Kindergarten.

name: Follotrimmen 8. løp
description: The Follotrimmen is a running carousel consisting of 8 races at various locations in Follo, featuring different distances, surfaces, and course profiles. This unique sports social event is perfect for those who want to experience the joy of running together with colleagues and friends. You can choose whether to participate for time or simply complete the distances, and here you can compete against yourself or measure your strength against other runners.
course_highlights: The Follotrimmen is a unique sports social event, perfect for those who want to experience the joy of running together with colleagues and friends.
Here you can compete against yourself or measure your strength against other runners.
The atmosphere at the Follotrimmen is as always great, both before, during, and after the race, and it's just to be enjoyed.

name: Mosvannsløpet
description: The Mosvannsløpet is organized by the Skjalg Sports Club and will take place on September 3, 2025. There are two distances: a children's race of approximately 500m at 5:00 PM and the main race of 3.05 km at 6:00 PM.
course_highlights: The race takes place on September 3, 2025.
Children's race of approximately 500m at 5:00 PM.
The main race of 3.05 km at 6:00 PM.

name: Land Løpskarusell
description: From April 30 to mid-September, the running series in Land is back. The Land Running Series 2025 includes 12 races, starting with a cross-country race at Lyngstrand on Wednesday, April 30. The final race will take place at Lands Museum on Wednesday, September 18. The races are suitable for both children and adults, and are designed for both recreational runners and competitive athletes, with several alternative distances available. There is also a recreational class without timing, and there is no license requirement for this class.
course_highlights: The Land Running Carousel is an initiative organized by Søndre Land IL Athletics and the athletics group in Nordre Land IL.
The races are suitable for both children and adults, and just as good for recreational runners as for competitive athletes.
Several alternative distances are offered in all the races.

name: Holavatnet Rundt 14
description: The Summer Carousel Holavatnet Round was first organized in 1983 and is now in its 41st season. On average, about 130 people show up every Wednesday to exercise or test their fitness in the scenic course. The route goes around Holavatnet on asphalt and gravel paths, and it is also possible to bring a stroller on the loop.
course_highlights: The course is 3.1 km long, with 1.1 km of asphalt, 1.8 km of gravel road, and 0.2 km of asphalt.
There is a nature trail for children in the hiking class, with a prize at the "cabin" at about 450 meters above sea level.
The race starts at about 40 meters above sea level, and the summit/finish is at 553 meters above sea level.

name: Bykarusellen Perseløp 3
description: Welcome to the second race of the season in the City Marathon Perseløp 2023! The date is May 24th and the distance is 5 km! The start and finish are at Marineholmen by VilVite, with a mass start at exactly 6:00 PM. The race features a certified course, pace setters, and there will be prizes for winners and a raffle from Löplabbet. Bring your friends, colleagues, family members, or good training partners and join the race!
course_highlights: Controlled course and pacers.
Winner and draw prizes from none other than Löplabbet!
Mass start at 6:00 PM at Marineholmen by VilVite.

name: Semsvannsrunden
description: The Semsvann Round is a unique running competition that takes you through beautiful scenic areas around Semsvannet. The loop around the lake is 4.6 km long and is hilly, featuring both gravel paths and forest trails. This is an accessible event where both walkers and runners can participate, either with or without timing. The start and finish are at the NaKuHel center, which also has Smia Café offering food and drinks. We hope for nice weather and a great atmosphere, so save the date for Wednesday, September 3rd!
course_highlights: The course runs partly on gravel roads and forest trails, and on the way around the lake, you pass both Tveiterfossen and Tveiter farm.
We plan for participants to either walk or run, with or without timing, with categories for both competition and personal improvement.
There will be food and drink for sale at Smia Café, where you can buy waffles, cake, rolls, soda, and coffee.

name: Smidalen Terrengløp
description: The Smidalen Trail Run was held for the first time on June 13, 2024, and will become an annual race in Smidalen and along the Nidelv Trail at Sluppen. Lush and unknown, Smidalen lies like a wooded belt along the Nidelva, with paths to run on and undiscovered climbing trees. This must be Trondheim's hidden valley.
course_highlights: Lush and unknown: Along the Nidelva, Smidalen lies like a forested belt, with trails to run on and undiscovered climbing trees.
The Sluppen Race was held for the first time on June 13, 2024, and will become an annual event in Smidalen and along the Nidelv Trail at Sluppen.

name: Saudasjøen Rundt
description: Saudasjøen Rundt 2024 will take place on September 7 from 11:00 AM to 3:00 PM. The courses include a main course of 5.3 km, a middle course of 2 km, and a separate children's race of 1 km, allowing everyone to participate. The race starts and finishes at Risvoll Skule in Saudasjøen, with parking available in the gravel lot below the school. There will also be a café offering coffee and cakes at the school.
course_highlights: The course of 5.3 km is short enough for everyone to participate, and there is also a middle course of 2 km.
There is a separate children's race of 1 km.
At school, there will be a café with coffee and cakes☕️🍰.

name: Gjerpenhavna 2.5 km Barneløp
description: Running in the woods and on trails is so much fun! Let's meet for some enjoyable running, whether the goal is the journey itself or to run as fast as possible. This race is for all children, from the time they can run up to the year they turn 14. The courses mainly go on trails, featuring both uphill and downhill sections, and it's allowed to jump in the puddles! The races are free, and on-site registration is possible up to 15 minutes before the start. Everyone receives a bib number, and at the finish line, there will be juice and a medal waiting.
course_highlights: The trails mostly run on paths and include both uphill and downhill sections.
The races are free, and you can sign up by following the link below.
At the finish line, there will be juice and a medal.

name: Dogrun - Hamar
description: VOM DOGRUN is for everyone who wants to participate in a pleasant activity with their dog. You can choose to compete with or without timing, and all participants receive a medal. The competitive class is approximately 6.2 km with timing, while the open class is about 3.1 km without timing. Additionally, there is a special activity for puppies, VOM PUPPY WALK, which is free to register for.
course_highlights: VOM DOGRUN is a social activity for both dogs and their owners.
One can participate in the competition class with timing or the open class without timing.
Participant medal for everyone.

name: Sparebanken Norge Stafett
description: The Sparebanken Norge Relay is a relay race consisting of 5 legs, where each leg is between 300m and 1500m. This event promotes social team building and improved public health. Join good colleagues, form a team, and participate in a short and intense relay together. How about challenging others in your own or competing businesses?
course_highlights: The Sparebanken Norge relay is a relay with 5 legs.
Each stage is between 300m – 1500m.
The Sparebanken Norge Relay is social team building and better public health combined in one event.

name: Knarvik Halvmaraton
description: Knarvik Half Marathon starts and finishes in the same place inside Knarvik Stadium. The course runs on roads in Knarvik and into the Brekkeløypa, where there is gravel, while the rest of the course is on asphalt. There are 8 aid stations along the route, and after crossing the finish line inside the stadium, water and bananas will be served. The course is well marked with approximately 20 course marshals present, and the Red Cross will also be on-site. The half marathon consists of 4 laps of the 5 km course, with an additional distance of 1097 meters onto the walkway towards Gjervik.
course_highlights: The course is car-free and offers participants beautiful scenery along the way.
There are 8 aid stations along the course, and after finishing, water and bananas will be served.
The age limit for participation is 15 years.

name: Knarvikmila 10/5/3 km
description: The Knarvikmila 3 km has its start and finish at Knarvik Stadium, and the course runs on roads in Knarvik and into Brekkeløypa, where there is gravel. The rest of the course is on asphalt, with one water station along the way. The course is well marked, car-free, and the Red Cross will be present for safety. The date of the race is Saturday, September 6, starting at 1:30 PM.
course_highlights: The course is easy, accurately measured, and there are cash prizes for the top 3 women and men.
Prizes will be awarded to all class winners, including youth/junior and veterans.
After finishing, participants receive water and bananas inside Knarvik Stadium.

name: Track & Glow 10k
description: Track & Glow 10k is organized at Gjesdal Sports Park, which is the second running track in Norway with Wavelight technology. Heat and wave setup will be announced soon, and lap counting will occur automatically in EQ-timing's system, which will display on the big screen how many laps you have completed. This race offers a unique opportunity to experience running with modern technology in a beautiful setting.
course_highlights: The second running track in Norway with Wavelight technology.
Lap counting will occur automatically in EQ-timing's system.
Heat and heat setup will be coming soon here.

name: Fauske Backyard Ultra
description: Fauske Backyard Ultra is an exciting backyard race where participants run a lap of 6.7 km up to twelve times. The race starts and ends at a gathering place with a food station, restrooms, and seating. Laps begin every full hour, and your pace determines how long of a break you get before the next start. The goal is to reach 80.4 km, but you are welcome to run as many laps as you wish or can handle.
course_highlights: Backyard running is a loop of 6.7 km that is run up to twelve times.
The laps start every full hour, and your pace determines how long of a break you get before the next start.
Even though the ultimate goal is to reach 80.4 km, you are warmly welcome to run as many laps as you want – or can manage.

name: Numedalsløpet
description: The Numedalsløpet was first held in 1936 and is thus one of the oldest sports events in Numedal. The race takes place on easy forest terrain from Høgheim in Lyngdal to Flesberg Community House and is approximately 13 km long. It is a race for both competitive runners and recreational joggers, organized in collaboration with Lyngdal and Svene Sports Clubs.
course_highlights: The race was first held in 1936 with 100 participants and has a long history.
The Numedalsløpet has a distance of approximately 13 km and takes place in easy forest terrain.
It is a race for both competitive runners and recreational participants, making it accessible for all levels.

name: Romsdalseggenløpet
description: The Romsdalseggen Race is a mountain run set in majestic surroundings, starting in Vengesdalen and finishing at the top of Nesaksla. During the journey across the mountain, you can expect both a thrilling sensation in your stomach and lactic acid in your legs, but above all, a fantastic experience with magnificent peaks like Vengetindene, Romsdalshorn, and Trolltindene surrounding you. The course is 8.6 km long, with 970 meters of positive elevation gain and 700 meters of negative elevation, and features exciting and challenging sections equipped with safety measures for secure passage.
course_highlights: The route offers a fantastic view with magnificent mountains such as Vengetindene, Romsdalshorn, and Trolltindene.
The course includes 4 different secured sections with chains to help participants navigate the challenging areas.
The exciting and challenging part begins when you reach the ridge, with 4.6 adrenaline-pumping kilometers remaining.

name: Furusjøen Rundt-løpet
description: The race starts at Rudland Fjellsenter and goes 500 meters on asphalted road towards Bjørgebu. Then the route follows Peer-Gynt Seterveg and turns towards Årvillingen, before it goes through easy, flat terrain along Årvillingen and further towards Hovde on gravel road to the first aid station. The route continues towards Fryosen and Frylisætra, and further to Luseby, Glitra, and Pungen, where the second aid station is located. After several gravel roads and scenic surroundings, the race concludes at Rudland Fjellsenter.
course_highlights: Trail running in enchanting surroundings, with a dedicated course for children and recreational runners.
Fun runs that can also be done as a march - for those who find it adventurous to be outdoors in beautiful nature alone or with friends, family, or colleagues.
The course follows a gravel road for about 3 km up towards Haugsetra, passing old mountain farm cabins, before descending again via Rustugusetra towards the finish.

name: Elvelangsløpet
description: The Elvelangsløpet 2023 takes place on Saturday, September 9, and invites you to an exciting race on the new hiking trail in Ål. The course is 4000 m long with small elevation changes, and there are separate courses for children and youth. The event includes distances of 400 meters for children, 1400 meters for youth, and 4000 meters for juniors, seniors, and veterans. The start and finish are at the new athletics track at Bråta, and participation is free with simple prizes.
course_highlights: Course record: Ladies 15:45 (Olivia Opheim) and Men 12:58 (Jonas Grøsland).
The event has a dedicated course for children and youth with distances of 0.4 km and 1.4 km.
The distribution of race numbers takes place right by the start at Bråta, with parking available.

name: Totens Tøffeste
description: The obstacle course race "Totens Tøffeste" will be held for the seventh time in Gjøvik on Saturday, August 31, 2024, after having over 1500 participants in 2023! The course for 2024 is just as tough and fun as always, with a length of approximately 6 km and over 40 challenging obstacles. It is designed so that everyone can finish and experience a sense of achievement, with the option of 5 burpees as an alternative if an obstacle is too difficult. You can participate individually or as a team, and choose your starting wave and time.
course_highlights: You will encounter a series of challenging and fun obstacles, with plenty of elevation gain over a distance of about 6 km.
The course is designed so that everyone can finish and that everyone will definitely experience a sense of achievement.
Everyone can decide for themselves whether they want to run with or without timing.

description: Orre Idrettslag is organizing Pølsemilå in collaboration with Håland Kjøtt. Pølsemilå 2025 will take place on September 6th at 2:00 PM, with the hike and children's race starting at 1:00 PM. Tickets for the event are purchased on-site, not online, and pick-up of race numbers will take place right outside Håland Kjøtt from 11:00 AM until the starting gun goes off.
course_highlights: Pølsemilå 2025 will take place on September 6th at 2:00 PM.
The hike and the children's race start at 1:00 PM.
Pick-up of race numbers takes place right outside Håland Kjøtt from 11:00 AM.

name: Jentemila
description: The Girls' Mile Bislett is Norway's most enjoyable women's race, and on September 5, 2026, it will be an unforgettable day with fantastic entertainment, shopping, running, and not least, a goodie bag and bubbles waiting for you when you cross the finish line! The Girls' Mile is a low-threshold race that includes everyone, and you can choose whether you want to run or walk, 5 or 10 km! We promise you the ultimate running party!
course_highlights: Fantastic atmosphere and great running conditions at Bislett Stadium!
You get beautiful running routes in idyllic surroundings.
Bubbly refreshment after the race and a goodie bag await you!

name: Accountor Hammerfestmila
description: Kvalsund Arctic Runners Running Club and Hammerfest Ski Club are joining forces to organize the new Hammerfest Mile. The date for the race is set for Saturday, September 6, and the event will take place in downtown Hammerfest. Choose between 10k, 5k, or a corporate relay (600 m per leg) where companies or groups of friends can have fun together. There will also be a children's race with free registration, and the start and finish will be at Rådhusplassen.
course_highlights: Choose between 10k, 5k, or corporate relay (600 m per leg).
There will also be a children's race with free registration.
Start and finish at Rådhusplassen.

name: Bodøryggen
description: On Saturday, October 1st, the Bodø Run Bodøryggen will take place, a majestic mountain race of approximately 21 kilometers from Skaug on the Nordsia of Bodø to Bestemorenga in the heart of Bodømarka. This mountain race features an elevation gain of 1000 meters, and the maximum number of participants is 200. The course is officially measured, and the steep ascent to Skaugtuva (626 m.a.s.l.) offers a fantastic view that can be enjoyed along the Bodøryggen.
course_highlights: Bodøryggen is a community festival featuring races and programs for everyone, local food and drinks, saunas and sea baths, music, entertainment, and simply a great northern Norwegian atmosphere!
The trail is well marked, but due to the length and elevation differences, sturdy hiking shoes and necessary gear such as water, snacks, and weather-appropriate clothing are recommended.
A fantastic run of 21.5 km with a view all the way.

name: Drammen Halvmaraton
description: Welcome to the Drammen Half Marathon – a spectacular running adventure that takes you through the lightning-fast 10-kilometer loop, twice! The Drammen Half Marathon has its roots in the 40-year-old Drammen Marathon, and Sturla Athletics has proudly organized this event in the city for 40 years. In the autumn of 2022, the race emerged with a new look and a faster route along the main road in Drammen.
course_highlights: Drammen Half Marathon is a spectacular running adventure that takes you through the lightning-fast 10-kilometer loop, twice!
The Drammen Half Marathon has its origins in the 40-year-old Drammen Marathon.
The race has a faster course on the main road in Drammen and new producers for the event itself.

name: Vestfold Marathon
description: Vestfold Marathon offers a marathon at 42.195 km, as well as a half marathon at 21.098 km. Participants can also take part in a relay, consisting of 8 legs for the marathon and 4 legs for the half marathon. The marathon starts in Larvik from the Hegdal Industrial Area, while the half marathon starts from Torp station in Sandefjord. There is an option for participation with a wheelchair, and water and energy drinks are provided at the aid stations.
course_highlights: Participants receive a medal upon completion, and there are prizes for the best in the competition.
The marathon relay team consists of 8 legs, while the half marathon relay team has 4 legs.
There is an opportunity for participation with a wheelchair, making the race accessible to more people.

name: Balestrand Opp og Rundt
description: Balestrand Up and Around 2025 is a timed competition that stretches over 9 km, starting and finishing at Kreklingen Stadium. The route goes from Kreklingen Stadium up to about 400 meters above sea level, where there is a relatively flat path to the day cabin "Balabu" and further to Fjærestadstølen. After that, the route descends on a developed path and forest road before returning to Kreklingen Stadium. Additionally, there is a non-timed fitness class of 6 km, where participants can choose their start time between 09:00 and 11:30 on Saturday, September 6th.
course_highlights: The trail goes from Kreklingen Stadium up to about 400 meters above sea level, with a relatively flat path to the day cabin "Balabu" and further to Fjærestadstølen.
There will be a ceremony for all participants near the starting point at around 4:00 PM.
Participants in the fitness class can register and choose a start time between 09:00 and 11:30.

name: Reistadtråkket
description: Reistadtråkket / Dølatråkket 2024 will take place on Saturday, September 7, featuring a trail run and hike of 15 km from Rabbåsen in Sørreisa municipality to the old Skoelv Bridge in Nedre Bardu. The race goes through beautiful hiking terrain with a mix of forest roads, paths, and varied landscapes. It has traditionally been held as a hike since 1997 but introduced its first competitive class in 2012. Participants compete in age-specific and gender-segregated categories, with awards for the top performers in each category.
course_highlights: The race takes place in beautiful hiking terrain on a mix of forest roads, trails, and off-road paths.
Competitions are held in age-specific and gender-segregated classes, with prizes for 1st to 3rd place.
Reistadtråkket is part of the Reistadtrippelen, which also includes the Reistadløpet and Gran Fondo Strade Statskog Blåtind.

images.alt_text: Reistadtråkket logo with runner profile and symbols for sport.

name: Sherpatrappa Opp
description: Sherpatrappa Opp is a rock-solid stair race organized by Northern Runners in Tromsø. The race ascends Sherpatrappa, a stone staircase in Tromsdalen that starts at Fløyvegen on the height of Lilleaksla and zigzags up the mountain until it ends at the radio mast on the plateau by Fjellheisen. The staircase, built by Nepalese sherpas from 2016 to 2019, has 1203 steps and offers participants a unique challenge. The event takes place on Saturday, September 7, 2024.
course_highlights: The Sherpa staircase has 1203 steps.
The staircase was built in stages from 2016 to 2019 by Nepalese mountain workers from a small village in Nepal.
The race is organized by Northern Runners and is known as Tromsø's toughest stair race.

name: Finnskogløpet

Around 2000 participants from all over Scandinavia take part, and Blodslitet has established a strong reputation as a top-quality event.
